semantic_summary: This dataset details current geographic buffers surrounding gas stations. It tracks the precise buffer distance in feet and calculates the total area in square miles for each buffered zone. Users can determine the total land area within the 1000-foot buffer zones surrounding gas stations across the city.

description: Feature layer generated from running the Create Buffers analysis tool.
semantic_summary: This dataset details one-mile buffer zones around gas stations. It tracks the calculated buffer distance in miles and the total area of each buffer zone in square miles. Users can query specific buffer distances and total areas to identify locations within one mile of a gas station.

description: Top 10 tree species for Denver Parks and Recreation's Office of the CIty Forester's 2022 Annual Report. The top 10 species include ash, maple, oak, honeylocust, pine, elm, linden, apple, hackberry, and spruce trees.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides information on Denver Parks and Recreation's top 10 tree species from their 2022 Annual Report. It includes detailed inventory and inspection data for ash, maple, oak, honeylocust, pine, elm, linden, apple, hackberry, and spruce trees in parks and public rights-of-way, tracking attributes like species, size, condition, disease defects, risk rating, and location. This data helps users analyze tree health, identify at-risk trees by disease or structural defect, and locate specific species by address, neighborhood, or park.

description: Most updated version as of 2/22/2024. Showing 2022 plantings and removals, data gathered from Treekeeper.

It tracks tree species, size, condition, defects, risk ratings, and locations via common and botanical names, diameter at breast height, neighborhood, and address, alongside owner details and equity scores for development projects. This data enables analysis such as identifying neighborhoods with the most ash tree removals or new plantings, or assessing tree health and green infrastructure impact by district.

description: Copy of DEDO 2022 NEST Neighborhoods layer
semantic_summary: This dataset defines the 2022 NEST Neighborhood boundaries for the City of Denver. It tracks individual neighborhood names and their geometric boundary lengths. Users can identify specific neighborhoods and retrieve their corresponding boundary dimensions.

description: 2023 Council Districts with Voting Population and Demographic data This layer contains Denver's City Council Districts as they were defined during the redistricting process approved on March 29, 2022. These districts were adopted in 2022 via an ordinance amending Article II of Chapter 15 of the Revised Municipal Code for purposes of approving a new redistricting plan for the eleven council districts of the City and County of Denver for the municipal election on April 4, 2023, and for any general or special council election held thereafter. This layer also contains demographic information for the newly-adopted council districts provided by the 2020 Decennial Census.

description: 2023 Paving Analysis
semantic_summary: This dataset details the City of Denver's 2023 street paving analysis and related transportation infrastructure planning. It tracks street segments by full name, length, and traffic attributes like volume, functional class, speed limits, and High Injury Network scores, alongside details on 2023 paving commitments, existing facilities, and recommended bike infrastructure including installation years and funding sources. This data can answer questions such as which streets are committed for 2023 paving, their High Injury Network scores, or details on existing and recommended bike facility installations and funding.

description: Feature layer for Plantings and Removals web map. Data represents tree plantings and tree removals in Denver from 2023 for Denver Parks and Recreation (DPR)'s Office of the City Forester's 2023 Annual Report. This feature layer is used in the Office of the City Forester (OFC)’s 2023 Annual Report, shared via StoryMaps. This data includes tree plantings and tree removals. These plantings and removals are further separated by city initiated removal/planting compared to development, or private, removal/planting. Data gathered via TreeKeeper. Final edits performed 3/20/2024.
semantic_summary: This dataset details 2023 tree plantings and removals managed by Denver's Office of the City Forester, distinguishing between city-initiated and development-related activities. It tracks common species, size class, geographic coordinates, inspection dates, and additional details like owner information and equity scores across various city districts and neighborhoods. Users can analyze tree activity by species, size, location, and responsible party, for example, identifying which neighborhoods received the most city-initiated plantings or the equity score of specific removals.

description: Top 10 tree species for Denver Parks and Recreation (DPR)'s Office of the City Forester (OFC)'s 2023 Annual Report
semantic_summary: This 2023 dataset identifies the top 10 tree species managed by the Denver Parks and Recreation Office of the City Forester. It details common species names, size classes, work groups, districts, and geographic coordinates for species like ash, maple, and oak, with inspection dates available for some. Users can query the distribution and density of specific tree species by size class within Denver's park districts, for instance, to find where most honeylocust or elm trees are located.

description: ARPA

Users can analyze which neighborhoods exhibit higher proportions of struggling populations or specific health challenges to understand disparities and inform resource allocation.

Use this data to identify neighborhoods or areas with specific economic, health, or education needs based on their 2024 index scores.

This dataset details the 2024 Phase 1 sanitary sewer lining projects. Users can identify pipes by FACILITYID, determine their lining type and dimensions, and find lining and inspection dates for specific project phases.

description: 2024 Phase 2 Sanitary Lining
semantic_summary: This dataset details the 2024 Phase 2 sanitary sewer lining projects within the City of Denver. It tracks essential pipe characteristics like diameter and length, lining type, installation and inspection dates, along with comprehensive notes on liner condition, safety, and curing logs. Users can query this data to identify specific pipe segments lined in 2024, determine their diameter and length, and assess their final liner condition.

This dataset details the 2024 Phase 2 sanitary sewer lining projects. It tracks facility IDs, pipe dimensions, lining types, installation and inspection dates, liner condition, and operational details including traffic control and bypass information. Users can query specific pipe segments to determine their lining type, installation date, current condition, and associated project details.

It includes attributes such as facility ID, depth, ground elevation, rehabilitation type, rehab and inspection dates, liner thickness, and detailed rehab notes and post-visual inspection results. This data allows users to identify which manholes were rehabilitated, the specific rehabilitation methods and dates, and assess post-rehab conditions or liner thickness.

This dataset details manhole rehabilitation efforts for Phase 1 of 2024. It tracks facility IDs, depth, ground elevation, rehabilitation type, rehabilitation date, inspection dates, and associated comments for individual manholes. Users can identify manholes by facility ID, determine rehabilitation types and dates, or retrieve inspection details and physical dimensions.

It tracks both city-managed and development-related tree actions, including species (common and botanical), address, neighborhood, size, and details like inspection dates or equity scores. Users can analyze which tree species were planted or removed by city crews versus developers, and evaluate these activities by neighborhood, district, or for their impact on equity.

It tracks recommended facility types, total bike and road lengths in miles, installation year and mechanism, funding sources, and project phases for each initiative. Users can identify current bike projects, their funding sources, project phases, and recommended facility types for planning purposes.

description: Top 10 tree species for Denver Parks and Recreation (DPR)'s Office of the City Forester (OCF)'s 2024 Annual Report
semantic_summary: This 2024 web map service provides tree inventory data for the City of Denver's top 10 tree species, as compiled for the Annual Report. It details individual tree characteristics, including common and botanical species names, diameter, condition, location information (address, neighborhood, park), and risk factors like EAB and structural defects. Users can analyze the distribution, health, and potential risks of these key tree species across Denver's parks and public spaces.

This dataset describes current and planned Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) infrastructure components across Denver. It details various device types like traffic controllers, detection systems, radio communications, network switches, and roadside units (RSUs), providing their geographic location, operational status, manufacturer, model, installation year, and project funding. This data is ideal for analyzing the distribution and operational status of ITS components, such as identifying all active roadside units (RSUs) or traffic controllers installed at specific street intersections, their status, and funding source.

Users can query this data to identify which 2025 Phase 2 manholes require specific rehabilitation types or to determine their physical dimensions like diameter and depth.

It delineates the precise geographic extent of these 50-foot buffer zones, indicating areas designated for habitat restoration and conservation along the river. This data can be used to identify properties or projects located within 50 feet of the South Platte River's riparian zones, informing planning and environmental assessments.

This dataset provides recent American Community Survey demographic and socio-economic data for Denver's branch service areas. It tracks population totals, racial and ethnic groups, gender, age ranges, educational attainment, household types, and foreign-born status for each service area. This data can answer questions such as "Which Denver branch service areas have the highest concentrations of specific age groups, educational attainment, or foreign-born residents?"

This dataset provides recent American Community Survey (ACS) demographic and socioeconomic data for defined City of Denver branch service areas. It tracks detailed population counts by race, ethnicity, age, and sex, alongside educational attainment, family households, and foreign-born status for each area. Users can analyze which service areas have specific population characteristics, such as the highest number of school-aged children or residents with a bachelor's degree.

This dataset provides current demographic data for City of Denver service areas. It tracks total population, racial and ethnic groups (Hispanic/Latino, White, Black, Native American, Asian, Hawaiian/Pacific Islander, Other, Two or More Races), and gender counts (Male, Female) for each designated branch or service area. What are the total population, racial, or gender demographics for a specific service area or branch within Denver?

description: Denver City Council Districts enriched with ESRI Demographic data from most recent ACS, Census, and Living Atlas sources.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides demographic data for Denver City Council Districts, featuring 2024 population estimates and 2022 language proficiency statistics. Data includes district numbers, current representatives, total population, and granular statistics on language spoken at home across age groups (5-17, 18-64, 65+) and English proficiency levels for Spanish, Indo-European, and Asian/Pacific Islander languages. This data can help answer questions like, "Which Denver City Council districts have the largest population aged 65+ who speak an Indo-European language and have limited English proficiency?"

This dataset contains American Community Survey (ACS) family demographics by service area. It tracks key attributes such as educational attainment levels (from less than high school to bachelor's or higher), counts of family households, and foreign-born populations. Use this data to analyze the distribution of educational attainment, family households, and foreign-born populations across different service areas.

description: ACS Language Indicators Neighborhood
semantic_summary: This dataset provides recent American Community Survey (ACS) neighborhood-level language indicators for Denver. It details neighborhood names, percentages of the population with Limited English Proficiency (LEP) by various languages (e.g., Spanish, Chinese, Vietnamese), foreign-born status, and socio-economic factors like median household income and poverty rates. This data enables analysis of language access needs, identification of areas with specific language support requirements, and understanding socio-economic disparities related to language proficiency within Denver's neighborhoods.

description: This data set should be used for planning and analysis of activities that are within the City and County of Denver. Neighborhood level data from the derived from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2017-2021. Data was aggregated at the census tract level, and the summarized into neighborhoods. This information was then joined with Community Planning and Developments Neighborhoods layer. This data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a census. Results should be considered estimates. Since this data was internally derived by the City and County of Denver from census tract level data, Margin of Error statistics from the census tract data could not be accurately aggregated for the neighborhood level data. Therefore, the Margin of Error data is not provided with this data set. Users should use caution as data values are estimates.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides Denver neighborhood-level American Community Survey data on the percentage of the population under 18 years old, averaged from 2017-2021. Key attributes include Neighborhood Name, Total Population All, Age Less than 18, and the calculated Percent Age Less Than 18. This data can be used to identify Denver neighborhoods with higher or lower percentages of residents under 18 for planning and analysis.

American Community Survey (ACS) current school enrollment statistics are provided by service area. It details total enrollment, plus specific counts for nursery/preschool, kindergarten, and grade ranges 1-4, 5-8, and 9-12, organized by Branch. This data allows users to analyze the distribution of students by grade level, for instance, determining kindergarten or high school enrollment in a specific branch.

This dataset presents American Community Survey (ACS) demographic data focused on youth populations within defined service areas. It tracks total population counts alongside specific age breakdowns for youth, including ages less than 5, 5 to 9, 10 to 14, and 15 to 17, all organized by service area 'Branch'. Users can analyze which service areas, identified by 'Branch', have the highest total youth populations or concentrations within specific age ranges like 5-9 or 15-17.

description: These data are the common data fields from the American Community Survey agreed upon by the Data Indicators GIS Subcommittee. It includes 2-9 unit structures data derived from the latest American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. The data source is Census Tract level data from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2019-2023. Data was aggregated at the census tract level, and the summarized into neighborhoods. This information was then joined with Community Planning and Developments Neighborhoods layer. This data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a census. Results should be considered estimates and be used for high level planning purposes only.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides neighborhood-level population, demographic, and housing indicators derived from the 2019-2023 American Community Survey 5-year estimates for the City and County of Denver. It tracks key metrics such as educational attainment, age distribution, housing cost burden, per capita income, poverty rates, vehicle access, disability status, household composition, racial/ethnic demographics, unemployment, and 2-9 unit structures. Use this data to identify Denver neighborhoods with specific demographic characteristics, such as areas with a high percentage of cost-burdened households or significant populations under 18 in single-parent families.

description: These data are the common data fields from the American Community Survey agreed upon by the Data Indicators GIS Subcommittee. It includes 2-9 unit structures data derived from the latest American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. The data source is Census Tract level data from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2019-2023. The original census tract group boundaries have been adjusted to various Denver GIS data layers to increase the spatial accuracy of this data. Although every effort was made to ensure the accurate rectification of the data, due to geographic problems inherent in the original 2010 census block group data, errors may exist. The data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a complete census. Data should be considered estimates and a margin of error table is located on the city network that can be used in conjunction with this dataset.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides Denver's population and housing indicators derived from the 2019-2023 American Community Survey 5-year estimates at the census tract level. Key attributes include educational attainment, median household income, poverty rates, population density, racial demographics, and housing characteristics like renter occupancy and vehicle access. Use this data to identify census tracts with high rates of poverty, unemployment, or households without vehicle access, and to analyze demographic breakdowns by age and race within Denver.

This dataset provides 2021 American Community Survey data on languages spoken at home within census tracts. It tracks total population, the count and percentage of speakers for languages like English, Spanish, French, Chinese, and Vietnamese, and identifies the dominant language per tract. Users can query this data to find census tracts with the highest percentage of non-English speakers or identify areas where specific languages are prevalent.

description: active trails projects 2021
semantic_summary: This dataset describes active trails projects for the City of Denver in 2021. It contains details for each 'Active Trail Project' including 'From' and 'To' locations, 'Length', 'Status', associated 'Website', 'Description', 'PM' (Project Manager), and 'Lead Agency'. Users can determine the 'Status' or 'Length' of specific projects, identify the 'Lead Agency', or find project websites for active trail initiatives within the city.

This dataset tracks the status of Phase 1 ADA barrier removal projects completed and in progress for the City of Denver. It details specific facilities by address, council district, and type, documenting their construction year, the number of barriers remediated, and ongoing removal progress. Users can identify which facilities in a specific council district have completed ADA barrier removal, or determine the planned completion year for in-progress remediations.

description: Additional Parcels for the Affordable Housing Map
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current property parcel information, including vacant land and parcels owned by various public entities, for the City of Denver's Affordable Housing Map. It tracks key attributes such as parcel identification numbers (PIN, SCHEDNUM), owner and situs addresses, land and improvement values, total property value, and property class. Users can leverage this data to find vacant properties or those owned by entities like the State of Colorado, RTD, DPS, or National Western, complete with ownership and valuation details for urban planning.

This dataset defines the administrative council districts for the City of Denver as they existed in 2015. It includes attributes detailing the district number, the assigned council representative, and any associated administrative notes. Use this data to identify specific council district boundaries, find a district's representative, or query by district number.

description: Park Maintenance Districts
semantic_summary: This dataset defines the current administrative boundaries for the City of Denver's park maintenance districts. It includes specific district names, assigned superintendents, and comprehensive contact information such as physical addresses, phone numbers, and fax details. Users can quickly identify the superintendent and full contact information for any particular park maintenance district.

Current data on adoptable trail segments in Denver. It tracks details such as Trail Name, Segment Name, TYPE_CLASS, Approximate Mileage, current Adoptee, and if the segment 'Needs Volunteers'. Users can identify which specific trail segments 'Need Volunteers' and their 'Approximate Mileage' for potential adoption.

description: Additional data requested to be added to the City Properties web application
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current geographical data related to transportation safety and flood risk within the City of Denver. It details high injury network segments for pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, linking them to demographic attributes such as age, disability, and proximity to schools, along with FEMA flood zones and special flood hazard areas. This data can answer questions about which road segments pose the highest injury risk for different modes of transport, how these risks correlate with vulnerable populations, or which properties fall within a designated flood zone.

description: Street Labels to go over the 2019 aerial imagery
semantic_summary: This dataset provides Denver street network and address label information, designed to overlay 2019 aerial imagery. It tracks detailed street segment characteristics including full names, prefix/type/suffix, address ranges (left/right, from/to), length in miles, speed limits, one-way status, number of travel lanes, and maintenance jurisdiction. Users can query this data to identify street full names, determine speed limits and one-way status for specific segments, or find the address ranges associated with particular road sections across Denver.

description: This map displays Affordable Housing by parcel, and all services and amenities, for use in locating new affordable housing developments.
semantic_summary: This dataset maps current Denver affordable housing developments, associated properties, and essential community amenities. It tracks property details, owner information, assessed values, facility specifics for various care types, services from workforce centers and schools, amenities like food stores, parks, and transit, plus contextual data including zoning and neighborhoods. Users can identify potential sites for affordable housing by analyzing parcel characteristics, existing facilities, and proximity to crucial services and transportation.

semantic_summary: This dataset provides contextual layers for analyzing air quality in Denver, integrating recent demographic, socioeconomic, and public health statistics. This data supports inquiries like, 'Which Denver census tracts or neighborhoods near industrial areas or major highways exhibit higher rates of asthma hospitalization, diabetes prevalence, or specific demographic profiles?'

This dataset provides comprehensive information on all permitted corrals as of January 2025. It tracks key details including corral permit numbers, owner names, precise location addresses with latitude/longitude, project titles, sizes, and descriptive notes for each entry. Users can query this data to identify specific corrals by owner or location, assess their size and descriptions, or understand their current permitting cycle status.

description: count
semantic_summary: This dataset details characteristics and financial information for businesses funded by the City of Denver, encompassing various award rounds and 2019 revenue. It tracks entity details including legal name, address, award amount, industry, MWBE ownership, employee counts, and 2019 gross revenue, alongside aggregated neighborhood statistics. This data can answer questions regarding funded business demographics, such as the distribution of award amounts, MWBE ownership, and employee counts by industry or Denver neighborhood.

semantic_summary: This dataset details Denver's urban environment, focusing on building characteristics, school properties, and solar shadow analysis, incorporating demographic data primarily from the 2010 U.S. Census. It tracks building height and type, school property details including full names, addresses, parking, and roof areas, combined with seasonal solar shadow patterns and comprehensive 2010 census demographics such as population, age, race, and housing units by tract. Users can analyze the impact of building shadows on school properties or parking areas, correlate mean building heights with 2010 population demographics, or identify schools with significant unshaded roof and parking space.

description: All layers for the story map in a single zoom
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current three-dimensional shadow frequency data for the City of Denver. It tracks various counts related to shadow presence, including general counts, roof-specific shadow counts, and comparisons between 2D and 3D shadow calculations across different surfaces. Users can determine which rooftops in Denver are most suitable for solar panel installation by analyzing specific shadow frequency counts, including 3D calculations.

This dataset provides current information on all Level 2 and 3 electric vehicle (EV) charging stations across the City of Denver. It includes details such as station name, street address, access times, accepted payment methods, types and counts of EV connectors, pricing, and the associated EV charging network. Users can inquire about charger locations, identify available Level 2 or DC fast charging ports, check access times, or find chargers associated with a specific EV network.

description: This layer shows the buffer area for all TB21 youth facing facilities, including private and public school area, recreation centers and swimming pools.

Users can query which types of youth facilities exist within a specified buffer area, their addresses, hours of operation, and offered programs.

description: All Walkshops
semantic_summary: This dataset provides information about all 'walkshops' as of March 21, 2023. The data tracks individual walkshops, primarily identified by a unique Walkshop ID (WID). Users can query this data to identify specific walkshops by their unique WID or retrieve a comprehensive list of all walkshop offerings.

description: Denver Animal Shelters that are open admission and have night drop
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current information on Denver's open admission animal shelters that offer night drop services. It tracks facility details including name, physical address, phone number, operating hours, and a descriptive overview for each location. This data helps users locate and contact open admission animal shelters in Denver, determine their hours, and understand available night drop services.

description: ATO23_MapData
semantic_summary: This dataset quantifies 2023 Access to Opportunity and Equity Scores across Denver neighborhoods. It tracks neighborhood-level data on social determinants of health, healthcare access, child morbidity, mortality, built environment, and transit access, providing composite Equity Scores. Use this data to analyze and compare neighborhoods based on their overall Equity Score, access to key services, or specific factors like child morbidity.

description: ATO24_MapData
semantic_summary: This dataset provides the City of Denver's 2024 Access to Opportunity and Equity Scores. It details neighborhood-level metrics such as social determinants of health, access to healthcare, child morbidity, mortality, built environment, food access, park access, poverty rates, education, and transit access. Users can analyze cumulative equity scores (EquityScore_avg9) to identify specific neighborhoods experiencing disparities in healthcare, transit, and overall opportunity within Denver.

description: Test layer to review potential changes to Blueprint Access To Opportunity.
semantic_summary: This dataset represents the City of Denver's 2024 Access To Opportunity scores. It tracks cumulative scores and individual metrics related to social determinants of health, access to healthcare, child morbidity, mortality, built environment, poverty, education, and transit access for various neighborhoods. Users can analyze neighborhood equity by comparing overall EquityScore_avg9, life expectancy, and specific scores for food access, park access, and transit access.

description: ATO25_MapData
semantic_summary: This spatial dataset provides Denver's Access to Opportunity scores and contributing factors, primarily focusing on a 2025 projection. It tracks neighborhood-level metrics including Social Determinants of Health, Access to Healthcare, Child Morbidity, Mortality, Built Environment, transit access, food access, park access, poverty rates, and education. This data can answer questions such as "Which Denver neighborhoods have the lowest EquityScore_avg9 or highest Pct_PopPoverty based on the 2025 projections?"

description: TEST
semantic_summary: This dataset provides comprehensive 2023 information on Denver's property parcels, demographic characteristics, and socio-economic indicators. It includes detailed property attributes like ownership, appraised values, zoning, and land area, combined with census tract data on high school graduation, family poverty, and various equity scores, including access to transit, food, parks, and healthcare. This data can answer questions such as how property values and zoning relate to neighborhood equity metrics, access to services, and specific socio-economic conditions like poverty levels or life expectancy.

description: Scooter trip ends for August 2025
semantic_summary: This dataset details scooter trip end locations for August 2025. It primarily tracks the geographic coordinates, specifically latitude and longitude, where individual scooter trips conclude. Use this data to analyze where scooter trips most frequently terminate, identifying popular drop-off zones by their precise latitude and longitude.

description: This map has layers for use in analyzing the best placement for automated speed cameras.
semantic_summary: This dataset compiles Denver traffic accident, speed citation, and high injury network data, with specific citation records spanning 2020-2024. It tracks comprehensive traffic accident details including road and light conditions, vehicle and driver actions, and injury/fatality counts, alongside high injury network crash rates and detailed speed citation locations and charges. This data helps identify optimal automated speed camera placements by correlating areas with high crash rates, high speed crash counts, serious injuries, and fatalities with existing speed citation patterns.

description: Destinations for Bicycle Wayfinding
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current and planned bicycle wayfinding destinations and facilities for the City of Denver. It tracks K-12 schools, neighborhoods, and both existing and recommended bike facilities, detailing attributes like Wayfinding Destination Name, SCHOOL_NAM, ADDRESS_LI, FACILITYID, INSTALL_YEAR, PLAN_YEAR, SUM_BIKE_LEN_MI, and FUNDING_SOURCE. Users can identify schools and neighborhoods designated as wayfinding points, query facility details such as bike length and installation year, and discover planned bicycle infrastructure projects and their funding sources.

description: Destinations for Bicycle Wayfinding
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current official bicycle wayfinding destinations for the City of Denver. It includes layers for point, linear, and area destinations, D-Route signage, Denver Parks, and Business Areas, detailing attributes like Name, Place Type, and Wayfinding Level. Users can query this data to find specific bicycle destinations, understand their classification, and determine their recommended wayfinding level.

description: Overlap of bike facilities with parks
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current and planned information regarding bike facilities and parks within the City of Denver. It tracks recommended and existing bikeways, including their names, installation/plan years, length in miles, and funding sources, alongside details for parks such as their formal name, type, acreage, and associated facilities. This data helps identify the spatial overlap of bike routes with parks, allowing users to query which facilities exist within or near specific park types and their respective maintenance or council districts.

This dataset describes Denver's current inventory of installed bike lines. It tracks facility IDs, installation year, methods, funding sources, project phases, and segment lengths for each bike line, including their 'from' and 'to' street names. Users can query this data to identify bike lines installed in specific years, determine their funding sources, or calculate total lengths between designated 'from' and 'to' streets.

description: Comments from Denver Moves: Bikes Update outreach.
semantic_summary: This dataset contains public outreach comments related to the Denver Moves: Bikes Update project. It tracks feedback submitted as point or line features, detailing when comments were 'Created on', their 'General Category', 'Comment' text, 'Up Votes', 'Down Votes', associated 'Project', overall 'Sentiment', and relevant 'Route'. Users can analyze public opinion and engagement for specific bike routes or projects by querying 'Sentiment' for 'Up Votes' and 'Down Votes' within different 'General Category' comments.

description: Bike and Scooter Rank 18 or higher using POP_AMERCMTYSVY20172021BLKGP_A parameters.
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies bike and scooter opportunity areas within Denver using demographic and socioeconomic data primarily from 2017-2021. It tracks block group level attributes such as household income, education levels, population age, vehicle availability, disability status, racial and ethnic demographics, and includes various derived ranks for these factors. This data answers which Denver block groups rank highest for bike and scooter opportunity, allowing users to pinpoint areas with specific socioeconomic characteristics that indicate demand.

description: Overlap of Recommended Bikeways and Parks
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies current and recommended bikeway infrastructure in relation to parks across the City of Denver, incorporating historical development dates. It details attributes such as facility IDs, existing status, installation and plan years, bikeway and road lengths in miles, park types, GIS acres, and specific park facilities and funding sources. This data can answer questions like which recommended bikeway segments intersect with specific parks, what are the `GIS_ACRES` of parks impacted by proposed routes, or which park `FACILITIES` are adjacent to existing bike paths.

This dataset provides current information on the City of Denver's bikeway infrastructure. It tracks individual bikeway segments, detailing their unique facility ID, installation year and method, funding sources, and their total bike and road lengths. Users can query this data to identify bikeway project phases, installation dates, or funding sources for specific segments within the city.

description: Building roofprints delineated from 2020 aerial imagery. CAPTURE CRITERIA: Building roofprint polygons are stereocompiled in 3D. Outlines of permanent, visible structures are captured at the corners of the roof (eave). Buildings with area greater than or equal to 48 square feet and over 5 feet in height are collected. Arms and indentations must be 2.5 feet or greater to be captured. Canopies, carport covers, and sheds are included. For multi-level commercial and/or industrial buildings, each level is captured as a unique record if the building is greater than or equal to 1000 square feet and the multi-level roof levels are greater than or equal to 400 square feet in area and over 5 feet in height. Each polygon is a separate record. Polygons that are part of the same building have the same building ID. For pitched roofs, the highest point is used to determine the building height. The lowest point is the common lowest point if the building is multi-level. ATTRIBUTION: Unique ID, Height (feet), Ground Elevation (feet), Building Type (Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Medical, Public, Garage/Shed, Parking Structure, Tank, Foundation/Ruin, Miscellaneous). Building addresses are available for project partners, courtesy of BuildingFootprintsUSA. CHANGE FEATURES: This dataset is an update to previously collected data. Features were originally delineated from 2014 aerial imagery, updated in 2016, and then again in 2018 to create this dataset. Examples of change that are captured include but are not limited to: new features, change in attribution, and modifications that reach or exceed the threshold for initial collection of this feature. Additions refer not only to truly new features in the built environment but also to features that are added based on a larger extent of capture. Please refer to extent shapefiles for 2014, 2016 and 2018 feature captures before doing change analysis. Modifications are marked even if only a small portion of the feature has been changed. A separate change layer is available to show only those features that were delineated in 2020. SOURCE DATA: This feature was compiled from DRCOG 2020 Denver Regional Aerial Photography Project (DRAPP) imagery. This imagery is 4-band RGBIR color orthoimagery with a GSD (Ground Sample Distance) of 0.5 foot for 3-inch imagery, 1 foot for 6-inch imagery, and 2 feet for 12-inch imagery. Imagery was collected in the spring with a Vexcel Ultracam Eagle aerial sensor. Imagery is projected in the State Plane Coordinate System, Colorado Central Zone using the Lambert Conformal Conic map projection parameters. Horizontal and vertical datums are NAD83(11) and NAVD88(GEOID12A), respectively.

description: This data set should be used for planning and analysis activities within the City and County of Denver to develop agency, department, or citywide indexes for the City and County of Denver. Using this data as the source for your index layer will help ensure that all city agencies are drawing from the same source data when building indexes. The goal is to help bring various agency and department based indexes in closer alignment with each other by having a common and agreed upon data source. For more information contact the Denver Data Indicators GIS subcommittee. Data was extracted, processes, and derived from the latest American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates. These data are the common data fields from the American Community Survey agreed upon by the Data Indicators GIS Subcommittee. The data source is Census Tract level data from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2019-2023. The original census tract group boundaries have been adjusted to various Denver GIS data layers to increase the spatial accuracy of this data. Although every effort was made to ensure the accurate rectification of the data, due to geographic problems inherent in the original 2010 census block group data, errors may exist. The data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a complete census. Data should be considered estimates and a margin of error table is located on the city network that can be used in conjunction with this dataset.

semantic_summary: This dataset provides a comprehensive air quality index for Denver, integrated with detailed demographic and health statistics. It tracks population demographics by race, age, and gender for Denver census tracts and neighborhoods, alongside health indicators such as heart disease mortality, asthma hospitalization rates, and proximity to CDOT highways and industrial or airport zones. This data can answer questions such as how air quality-related health outcomes correlate with specific demographic groups or land uses near highways and industrial areas within Denver.

description: CBMS Layers; service published 10/23/2025 as a backup of layers originally published to Portal
semantic_summary: This dataset provides comprehensive monthly client statistics for Denver's Department of Human Services (DHS) programs, alongside DHS service locations and neighborhood equity indicators, spanning from May 2022 to September 2025. It tracks DHS resource site addresses, service categories, and includes monthly client counts for Adult Financial, SNAP, TANF, and Medical Assistance programs by neighborhood, along with socio-economic metrics like poverty, unemployment, and food desert status. Users can analyze the spatial distribution of DHS services, identify neighborhood trends in client program enrollment over time, or correlate equity index factors with assistance program uptake across Denver.

This dataset provides topographic contour lines for the City of Denver from 2020. It features both 1-foot and 5-foot interval contour lines, detailing their elevation values and contour types. This data allows users to identify specific elevations, assess terrain, or analyze landform characteristics across the city.

description: Parcels owned by the CCD impacting the 200' SPR Buffer
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current official property parcel information for land owned by the City and County of Denver, specifically those impacting the 200-foot SPR Buffer. Key attributes include schedule number, owner name and address, situs address, property class, zoning, and detailed appraised, assessed, and taxable property values. Which City and County of Denver-owned parcels impact the 200-foot SPR Buffer, and what are their appraised total values and zoning classifications?

description: To show parcels within the City and County of Denver as they are represented graphically. The geometry of this data is not of survey quality and should not be used for survey purposes. It is for general reference purposes only.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides parcel information for the City and County of Denver as of December 2024. It includes parcel identification, owner and situs address details, property class, zoning, and appraised and assessed property values. Users can identify parcel ownership, locate properties by situs address, and retrieve associated property class, zoning, and value information.

description: To show parcels within the City and County of Denver as they are represented graphically. The geometry of this data is not of survey quality and should not be used for survey purposes. It is for general reference purposes only.
semantic_summary: This dataset details City and County of Denver parcels within an influence zone, representing their graphical representation for 2025. Key attributes include unique parcel numbers, owner names and addresses, situs addresses, property classification and zoning, along with appraised and assessed property values. Users can query this dataset to find owner names, situs addresses, zoning designations, or current appraised and assessed values for specific parcels.

description: The zoning boundaries layer is an integral part of the planning and zoning data in the City and County of Denver Geographic Information System. This data is used by the Planning Department in case review, enforcement, and long range planning. GIS data layers are accessed by personnel in most City departments for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. This layer represents the zoning boundaries for the City and County of Denver, Colorado. The zoning boundaries data layer is governed by ordinance and is only changed accordingly.
semantic_summary: This dataset defines the current zoning boundaries for the City and County of Denver. It tracks detailed zoning classifications, including district type, use, form, overlay districts, neighborhood context, permitted height, ADU status, and associated Planned Unit Development details. This data enables users to determine the current zoning district, allowed uses, building height, or ADU regulations for a specific property or area for planning and review.

Users can identify areas of social vulnerability by exploring population demographics, socioeconomic status, and housing composition to answer questions like "Which Denver census tracts or neighborhoods have the highest proportions of vulnerable populations based on poverty, age, and minority status?"

This dataset details CDOT projects within Denver as of March 5, 2020. It tracks project identifiers, specific routes with beginning and ending reference points, geographic coordinates, and associated transportation planning organizations. Which GO Bond projects are active, what is their current status, and how do their actual costs compare to the estimated budget by district or project type?

description: Development Review/Project Coordinator Districts
semantic_summary: This dataset contains current information on City of Denver Development Review Districts. It tracks specific administrative development review areas, identifying the assigned project managers, their phone numbers, email addresses, and additional notes for each district. Users can query this data to find the project manager and contact details for a particular development review area or view district-specific notes.

This dataset provides current digital land area and boundary features for the City of Denver. It tracks unique feature identifiers or classifications, along with the precise perimeter lengths and calculated surface areas for each digital land unit. How can I identify land units by classification code or determine the precise perimeter and area of specific digital land features?

This dataset provides current geographic information system (GIS) data for property parcels within the City and County of Denver. It details owner names, complete owner and situs addresses, parcel identification numbers, tax districts, and assessed land and improvement values. This data allows users to answer queries like "What is the assessed land value and property class for a specific parcel, and who is the current owner?"

This dataset details Denver Human Services (DHS) locations as of July 2022. It tracks location details including service categories, complete street addresses, city, state, county, zip code, and other pertinent location descriptions. Users can query this data to find specific DHS locations by address or discover all locations offering a particular service category within a given zip code.

This dataset details Denver's neighborhood resource sites as of July 2022. It tracks the name, address, and geographic coordinates for each identified resource site. Users can locate specific resource sites by name or address, or identify sites within a particular geographic area.

This dataset represents 2022 aggregated branch service areas. This dataset represents future city planning blueprints for Denver. The data tracks individual future planning areas, providing their count and total area in square miles. Users can analyze the size of proposed future planning zones or determine the total area in square miles designated for new development.

This dataset summarizes Public Works Development Services Projects for the City of Denver. description: Distressed areas within the Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Area (NRSA)
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies current distressed areas within Denver's Neighborhood Revitalization Strategy Areas (NRSAs). It tracks the geographic boundaries and designations of these areas, providing spatial information relevant to urban planning. Users can query this data to locate specific distressed neighborhoods or analyze the spatial distribution of revitalization needs within NRSA boundaries.

description: District 10 Voter Locations with Neighborhood
semantic_summary: This dataset details current voter locations within Denver's District 10. It includes attributes such as State Voter ID, full residence address details (including longitude and latitude), associated neighborhood names, and neighborhood typology. Use this data to identify specific voter addresses and their corresponding neighborhood within District 10, or analyze voter distribution by neighborhood typology.

This dataset provides a map of existing diversion facilities. It tracks key information for each facility, including its type, name, exact location, phone number, and official website. Users can quickly locate specific types of diversion facilities and access their contact details, such as phone numbers and websites.

Users can identify diversion facility locations, determine their specific type, or find contact information like phone numbers and websites.

Current map data details diversion facilities within Denver. It includes attributes like the facility's type, name, exact location, phone number, and website. This data helps users locate specific types of diversion facilities and access their contact information.

description: DME Database 5_Mile Buffer Layer
semantic_summary: This dataset details ongoing and planned City of Denver infrastructure projects within a 5-mile buffer zone. It tracks project names, descriptions, current phases, planned costs, asset class, improvement type, and a variety of scores including equity, affordability, mobility, safety, and environmental justice. Which planned infrastructure projects within a 5-mile buffer have the highest combined equity and sustainability scores, along with their associated costs and current phase?

description: DME Delivers- 2024 Projects going to procurement or construction
semantic_summary: This dataset provides comprehensive information on the City of Denver's 2024 infrastructure projects. It tracks details for sidewalk, transit, pedestrian, multimodal, bridge, signal, and bikeway construction, including project names, types, estimated costs, funding sources, current status, completion metrics, and impact scores for mobility, safety, and equity. This data enables users to assess the geographic location, financial commitments, and progress of various 2024 capital improvement projects and evaluate their alignment with city goals like enhanced mobility and equity.

description: DOTI Equity Model 2022 revision
semantic_summary: This dataset details the 2022 revision of the City of Denver's DOTI Equity Index. It quantifies demographic disparities using 2019 ACS 5-Yr data on household income below poverty, education levels, age distribution, vehicle availability, disability status, and racial and ethnic groups, ultimately providing an "EquityScore" and "EquityGroupRank." Users can query this dataset to identify Denver areas with the lowest "EquityScore" or highest "EquityGroupRank" to pinpoint communities facing the greatest socio-economic and demographic challenges.

This dataset details the condition and mobility infrastructure of Denver's neighborhoods, using 2010 demographic baselines. It tracks key infrastructure attributes including bridge and street pavement condition (NBI, PCI scores), crosswalk ratings (OCI), sidewalk length and gaps, and sanitary major basin conditions. Users can analyze which neighborhoods exhibit the lowest average pavement condition index (PCI), the most significant sidewalk gaps, or the poorest average crosswalk and bridge conditions.

description: Questions for the DAFNE team to review 2025-04-15
semantic_summary: This dataset inventories questions for DAFNE team review, with a target date of April 15, 2025. It details each question's text, completion status, associated Google Map year, relevant intersection, and field check status. Users can query this data to identify incomplete questions requiring a field check, or locate questions pertaining to specific intersections or Google Map years.

description: Downtown Denver Enforcement Tracking
semantic_summary: This dataset provides ongoing enforcement tracking for activities and inspections across Downtown Denver. It meticulously tracks details such as inspection dates, addresses, current enforcement status, application names, and various inspection types associated with each record. Users can leverage this data to identify enforcement actions by address or district, track inspection status, or analyze specific inspection types and their frequency within Downtown Denver.

description: Produced by EPA Compiled by DDPHE/SSBO on behalf of EQM Data Steward: David Wilmonth Created from EJScreen 2.32 State Percentiles Tracts - Overview and represents only Colorado Census Tracts . Requested by EQM for the EJScreen Data for South Broadway Corridor App - Overview . Every polygon represents a Colorado Census Tracts and the associated EJScreen comparing state data. From the EPA dataset: This feature service was updated on 09/04/2024 and reflects EJScreen 2.32*** EJScreen is an environmental justice (EJ) screening and mapping tool that provides EPA with a nationally consistent dataset and methodology for calculating "EJ indexes," which can be used for highlighting places that may be candidates for further review, analysis, or outreach as the agency develops programs, policies and other activities. The tool provides both summary and detailed information at the Census block group level or a user-defined area for both demographic and environmental indicators. The summary information is in the form of EJ Indexes which combine demographic information with a single environmental indicator (such as proximity to traffic) that can help identify communities living in areas with greater potential for environmental and health impacts. The tool also provides additional detailed demographic and environmental information to supplement screening analyses. EJScreen displays this information in color-coded maps, bar charts, and standard reports. Users should keep in mind that screening tools are subject to substantial uncertainty in their demographic and environmental data, particularly when looking at small geographic areas, such as Census block groups. Data on the full range of environmental impacts and demographic factors in any given location are almost certainly not available directly through this tool, and its initial results should be supplemented with additional information and local knowledge before making any judgments about potential areas of EJ concern. This feature service of EJScreen data is at the census tract geography and uses State percentiles for EJ Indexes, Environmental Indexes, and Demographic Indexes. The Housing Cost Burden column was sourced from the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool (CEJST) website . Requested by EQM. FOR VIEWING PURPOSES ONLY. This data is not dynamic and only reflects data as of 01/15/2025 . Data is only updated at the request of EQM . Data quality is good.

semantic_summary: EJScreen environmental justice data for Colorado Census Tracts is provided as of January 15, 2025. This dataset tracks demographic indicators such as total population, race, low income, and limited English speaking households, alongside environmental indicators like particulate matter, traffic proximity, and hazardous waste proximity. Users can identify Colorado census tracts with higher Environmental Justice Indexes by examining combined demographic and environmental burden scores to highlight communities for further review.

description: Produced by EPA Compiled by DDPHE/SSBO on behalf of EQM Data Steward: David Wilmonth Created from EJScreen 2.32 US Percentiles Tracts - Overview and represents only Colorado Census Tracts . Requested by EQM for the EJScreen Data for South Broadway Corridor App - Overview . Every polygon represents a Colorado Census Tracts and the associated EJScreen comparing national data. From the EPA dataset: ***This feature service was updated on 09/04/2024 and reflects EJScreen 2.32*** EJScreen is an environmental justice (EJ) screening and mapping tool that provides EPA with a nationally consistent dataset and methodology for calculating "EJ indexes," which can be used for highlighting places that may be candidates for further review, analysis, or outreach as the agency develops programs, policies and other activities. The tool provides both summary and detailed information at the Census block group level or a user-defined area for both demographic and environmental indicators. The summary information is in the form of EJ Indexes which combine demographic information with a single environmental indicator (such as proximity to traffic) that can help identify communities living in areas with greater potential for environmental and health impacts. The tool also provides additional detailed demographic and environmental information to supplement screening analyses. EJScreen displays this information in color-coded maps, bar charts, and standard reports. Users should keep in mind that screening tools are subject to substantial uncertainty in their demographic and environmental data, particularly when looking at small geographic areas, such as Census block groups. Data on the full range of environmental impacts and demographic factors in any given location are almost certainly not available directly through this tool, and its initial results should be supplemented with additional information and local knowledge before making any judgments about potential areas of EJ concern. This feature service of EJScreen data is at the census tract geography and uses U.S. percentiles for EJ Indexes, Environmental Indexes, and Demographic Indexes. The Housing Cost Burden column was sourced from the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool (CEJST) website . Requested by EQM. FOR VIEWING PURPOSES ONLY. This data is not dynamic and only reflects data as of 01/15/2025 . Data is only updated at the request of EQM . Data quality is good.

Users can identify Colorado census tracts with elevated EJ Indexes, such as for Particulate Matter 2.5 or Low Income, to pinpoint areas for environmental justice analysis and outreach.

description: ARPA eligible areas for metroDenver DPA program These data are the common data fields from the American Community Survey agreed upon by the Data Indicators GIS Subcommittee. The data source is Census Tract level data from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2017-2021. The original census tract group boundaries have been adjusted to various Denver GIS data layers to increase the spatial accuracy of this data. Although every effort was made to ensure the accurate rectification of the data, due to geographic problems inherent in the original 2010 census block group data, errors may exist. The data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a complete census. Data should be considered estimates and a margin of error table is located on the city network that can be used in conjunction with this dataset.

It tracks case numbers, types, priority, creation and closure dates, subject, description, status, origin, assigned agency, and precise geographic location including latitude/longitude, City Council District, Police District, and zone. Users can query the number of open or closed cases, their status, assigned agency, resolution, or type within specific City Council or Police Districts.

This dataset documents current and historical encampment reports for the City of Denver. It tracks report details including case number, status, priority, creation and closure dates, geographic location, assigned agency, resolution, site status, number of people sheltered, and site dimensions. This data can answer questions such as "Which City Council Districts have the most active encampments, and what is the average number of people sheltered at these sites?"

This dataset covers Denver's ongoing encampment trash collection services. It tracks survey details for collected trash, including the specific date, location name, and quantities of bags and other items removed. Users can inquire about the total number of bags or other items collected at specific encampment locations on particular dates.

This dataset documents current and ongoing site visits to encampments within the City of Denver. It tracks detailed observations per visit, including the encampment site, number of people, vehicles, and structures, visit status, category, and total score, along with creation and editing details. Users can query this data to understand the observed population and infrastructure at specific encampment sites, identify visit trends, or analyze the activities of different agencies.

description: Encampment Closure Areas - House 1000
semantic_summary: This dataset details ongoing Encampment Closure Areas within the City of Denver. It tracks Site Status, operational dates (Date Open, Date Closed, Posting Date, Move In Date), area metrics (sqft, city_blocks), the Name and Category of each area, Number of People Sheltered, and associated Police District. Users can identify the Site Status of specific closure areas, determine the Number of People Sheltered by Police District, or analyze area metrics like sqft and city_blocks.

This dataset provides current information on services provided at encampment locations within the City of Denver. It tracks the geographic Location of encampments and details available amenities such as Trash Pickup, Portolets, Hand Washing Stations, and Sharps disposal. Users can query this data to identify which encampment locations offer specific services like sharps disposal or hand washing stations.

This dataset details current operational focus areas for encampment resolution within the City of Denver. It tracks specific geographic areas, the number of people and structures present, key dates like posting and move-in, their status, and whether they are designated as "street to lease." Users can query which active encampment focus areas have a specific number of people or structures, or identify those with recent posting dates that are designated as "street to lease."

This dataset provides current and ongoing information on City of Denver encroachment projects. It tracks details for various encroachment types, including bicycle and small cell, capturing project IDs, names, descriptions, statuses, permit numbers, and associated legal and legislative documentation. Users can identify the current status of specific encroachment projects, their types, associated permits, or relevant council bills and ordinances.

semantic_summary: This GIS dataset details Denver's Equity Priority Buildings and related demographic and environmental factors, current as of February 2023. It tracks Denver buildings (including size and energy performance), detailed neighborhood demographics, social equity indicators like affordable housing and health statistics, and comprehensive environmental factors such as air quality, climate vulnerability, and lead exposure risk. This data enables analysis to identify Denver's most vulnerable communities and buildings, allowing users to find specific properties in census tracts with high social equity index ranks, energy burdens, or pollution for targeted climate action and resource allocation.

description: This layer is to be used by City and County of Denver staff during right-of-way project planning (such as OneBuild) to determine what type of green infrastructure is recommended for projects occuring on any street segment in the city. description: This is a filtered subset of the "Edge of Pavement 2018" open data layer. This layer displays areas identified as a median with a paved surface with interstate medians removed. Edge of pavement polygons delineated from 2018 aerial imagery. CAPTURE CRITERIA: Edge of pavement polygons are compiled in 2D. This dataset includes the edge of paved and unpaved streets and roads with width greater than or equal to 9 feet that are intended for street-legal vehicle use. A road or street is defined as having consistent material from edge to edge. The delineated edge is the flowline (i.e. lowest point in curb). Unpaved trails are not included in this layer. Paved road polygons take precedence over sidewalk polygons but unpaved roads do not. Medians are delineated by a curb or raised surface but not a paint line. A median is any section within a corridor that cannot be driven on. Medians can contain any ground cover (grass, concrete, gravel, plantings, etc) and includes traffic islands and islands in cul-de-sacs. ATTRIBUTION: Unique ID, Surface (Paved, Unpaved), Type (Corridor, Median). CHANGE FEATURES: This dataset is an update to previously collected data. Features were originally delineated from 2014 aerial imagery, updated in 2016, and then again in 2018 to create this dataset. Examples of change that are captured include but are not limited to: new features, change in attribution, and modifications that reach or exceed the threshold for initial collection of this feature. Additions refer not only to truly new features in the built environment but also to features that are added based on a larger extent of capture. Please refer to extent shapefiles for 2014, 2016 and 2018 feature captures before doing change analysis. Modifications are marked even if only a small portion of the feature has been changed. A separate change layer is available to show only those features that were delineated in 2018. SOURCE DATA: This feature was compiled from DRCOG 2018 Denver Regional Aerial Photography Project (DRAPP) imagery. This imagery is 4-band RGBIR color orthoimagery with a GSD (Ground Sample Distance) of 0.5 foot for 3-inch imagery, 1 foot for 6-inch imagery, and 2 feet for 12-inch imagery. Imagery was collected in the spring with a Vexcel Ultracam Eagle aerial sensor. Imagery is projected in the State Plane Coordinate System, Colorado Central Zone using the Lambert Conformal Conic map projection parameters. Horizontal and vertical datums are NAD83(11) and NAVD88(GEOID12A), respectively.

description: This data identifies the middle housing stock in the City and County of Denver. Middle housing stock is represented as parcel boundaries where the Denver Assessor Land Use Classification is any of the following: ⦁ residential, residential-4d, residential-4 to 8 units, residential-apartment, residential-condominium, residential-boarding home, residential-duplex, residential-multi unit apts, residential-rowhouse, residential-senior citizen apt, or residential-triplex. An estimated unit count for each middle housing stock parcel is based on the Denver Assessor’s Total Unit value. If there is no Total Unit value, a count of the Tenant Address Unit points within each parcel is used to estimate unit counts. If there are no Tenant Address Unit points within the parcel, the count of the Owner Address points were used. The dataset is static and limited to use by Community Planning & Development staff for analysis for the Unlocking Housing Choices project. Parcels within the City and County of Denver as they are represented graphically.
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies the City and County of Denver's middle housing stock based on a static 2025 snapshot of parcel data. It tracks parcel boundaries, estimated unit counts, owner and situs addresses, property classifications, zoning, appraised values, land area, and original construction year. Users can analyze the distribution of middle housing stock, its unit density within specific zoning areas, and key characteristics like property value or year built.

description: The dataset contains middle housing type parcels as they were represented graphically in March 2025 that were once single-family residential parcels in January 2010. 'Middle housing' and 'single-family residential' are based on the Denver Assessment Property Class Codes. Changes were identified using Denver Assessment Property Class Codes and changes in parcel boundaries. The dataset contains parcels that have changed from middle housing in 2010 to single-family homes in 2025, based on the Denver Assessment Property Class Code. 2010 Middle Housing: Parcels classified as one of the following as of January 2010: apartment unit w/comm, apt w/2 units, apt w/3 units, apt w/4 units, apt w/5 units, apt w/6 units, apt w/7 units, apt w/8 units, condominium, pbg all bldgs. 2025 Single-Family Residences: Parcels classified as one of the following as of March 2025: consists of parcel polygons, where the Denver Assessment Property Class Code as of March 2025 is any of the following: SFR Grade A, SFR Grade A or X, w/RK, SFR Grade B, SFR Grade B w/RK, SFR Grade C, SFR Grade C, D, or E, w/RK, SFR Grade D or E, SFR Grade X. The dataset was created for Community Planning & Development's Unlocking Housing Choices project. Parcel datasets as of January 2010 and March 2025 were used to investigate how parcel property class code classifications have changed. Parcels in this dataset are represented graphically as they were in the City and County of Denver Assessor Parcel database as of 2010. The dataset is static.
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies Denver parcels that transitioned from single-family residential to middle housing between January 2010 and March 2025. Users can analyze where and how single-family properties converted to middle housing, examining property characteristics, valuation changes, and ownership patterns for housing development projects.

description: DOTI Equity Model The Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (DOTI) developed the DOTI Equity Index to prioritize areas of need and capital allocation for projects. The Transportation Mobility Planning Division uses the Equity Index to determine Denver’s Priority Areas for Transportation Equity. The resulting data model uses a data-driven approach to evaluate areas of inequity by performing a weighted overlay analysis using demographic indicators that correlate with more historic disinvestment, which also indicates a higher reliance on active transportation and transit systems. The equity index is intended to be used with supplemental data to help provide a better overall picture for any given program. For example, the Vision Zero program will also use safety and vehicle crash data in unison with the equity index to help prioritize investment locations. The Equity Index is comprised of the following seven demographic characteristics: Race & Ethnicity Income & Poverty Education Level Populations of Age 65+ Households with No Vehicle Female Heads of Household People with Disabilities
semantic_summary: This dataset outlines the City of Denver's Department of Transportation & Infrastructure (DOTI) Equity Index for current prioritization and capital allocation. It tracks 'EquityScore' and 'EquityGroupRank' by aggregating seven demographic indicators, including 'Race & Ethnicity', 'Income & Poverty', 'Education Level', 'Households with No Vehicle', and 'People with Disabilities'. This data helps identify which Denver neighborhoods have higher 'EquityScore' and 'EquityGroupRank' to determine priority areas for transportation equity investment.

description: This dataset is a record of soil core sampling activity undertaken in support of various roadway and underground utility projects in the City and County of Denver. Users can identify specific soil types, depths, and moisture levels, as well as depth to water and pavement layers (asphalt, concrete) for particular street addresses or project areas.

description: This layer portrays boundaries of subdivided lands within the City and County of Denver. Denver-owned lands in other counties are not included in this dataset. description: This index is a visual representation of some of the socioeconomic, built environment, health care, and heath barriers that residents of Denver neighborhoods face in accessing opportunities to lead healthy, productive lives. This index presents data in a way that helps inform decision makers about where City investment and resources are needed most so that those living in Denver's underserved neighborhoods can reach their full potential. In this index, a lower score indicates higher inequity. Overall equity scores are made up of scores from each of the sub-indices (see description for indicators included in each sub-index). Symbology can be shown for either a particular sub-index or the overall equity score. This layer is an update of the 2017 version of the DDPHE Neighborhood Equity Index. There have been additional indicators added to this layer updated in 2020, so the 2017 and 2020 versions of the index will not be directly comparable. DDPHE recommends using a blue-yellow color scheme rather than a color that shows the nieghborhoods with highest inequity in red to avoid stigmatizing those neighborhoods. Indicators Included in IndexSocioeconomic IndicatorsPercent of population in poverty (2014-2018 American Community Survey)Percent population 25 and older without a high school diploma (2014-2018 American Community Survey)Built Environment IndicatorsPark Access – Percent of units within 10-minute walk of park (Denver Parks and Recreation, 2019)Food access – Percent population within 10-minute walk (based on walkshed/walk network) to a full-service grocery storePopulation estimates from 2010 census, food stores from 2020 listAccess to CarePercent of women who did not receive prenatal care in the first trimester (Vital Records, 2017)Percent of Adults who Delayed Medical Care Due to Cost (2014-2017 - CDPHE Community Estimates Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System)MorbidityPercent Childhood obesity (2014-2016, BMI Surveillance System)Percent Adult depression (2016, Colorado Health Observation Regional Data Service)MortalityYears of Average Life expectancy (2011-2015, U.S. Area Life Expectancy Estimates Project)Index Score Calculation Methodology:Each indicator was updated to its most recent year/year range.The percentage or rate/prevalence for each indicator at the neighborhood level was added to a spreadsheetNote that each indicator was put in the spreadsheet in its 'negative' form - so that a higher percentage is the worse outcome; this was done so that ranking and scoring could be done in the same direction and to keep with the previous version of the index where a low score indicates more inequity, and a high score indicates less inequity (see Step 3 about ranking to learn more)The percentage/raw data spreadsheet was loaded into Stata, then grouped, ranked, and scoredThe indicators for each sub-index were ranked separately by neighborhood, then each grouped into quintilesThe quintile group became the 'score' for each indicator. The scores for each indicator were averaged together to get the sub-index scoresOnce each sub-index score is created, all sub-index scores were averaged together to get the overall equity index score per neighborhoodA spreadsheet is exported from Stata and loaded into ArcGIS ProThe spreadsheet was matched to the neighborhood boundary shapefileEach sub-index, as well as the overall index scores, were mapped and saved as layer files
semantic_summary: This dataset presents Denver's 2020 Neighborhood Health Equity Index. It tracks neighborhood-specific average scores for socioeconomic status, built environment, access to care, morbidity, mortality, and an overall equity score, where lower scores indicate higher inequity. Which Denver neighborhoods have the lowest overall equity scores or specific sub-index scores, indicating areas most in need of city investment and resources?

description: This layer shows areas of limited food access by Denver neighborhood based on the proportion of the housing units within a 10 minute walk of a full service grocery store for 2025. Full-service grocery store is defined based on the size of the store and availability of healthy food options such as produce. This layer estimates neighborhood access based on living units within the 10-minute walkshed rather than using the proportion of the total neighborhood population within the walkshed, which better accounts for where people actually live within a neighborhood. It was joined with the most recent ACS Common Data Indicators provided by TS GIS (ACS 2018-2022). This layer is updated annually and the Data Steward is Liane Cidlowski in Community & Behavioral Health and The Department of Public Health and the Environment.
