description: The U.S. Small-area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP) project produced estimates of life expectancy at birth—the average number of years a person can expect to live—for most of the census tracts in the United States for the period 2010-2015. The U.S. Small-area Life Expectancy Estimates Project (USALEEP) is a partnership of NCHS, the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation (RWJF)External, and the National Association for Public Health Statistics and Information Systems (NAPHSIS)External to produce a new measure of health for where you live. The USALEEP project produced estimates of life expectancy at birth—the average number of years a person can expect to live—for most of the census tracts in the United States for the period 2010-2015. These estimates were published in September, 2018."A growing body of research is recognizing the importance of measuring mortality outcomes in small geographic areas, such as U.S. census tracts, to identify health disparities within a population. The indicator most widely identified as the ideal measure of a population’s mortality experience is life expectancy at birth. The concept of life expectancy is intuitive and easily understood by both policymakers and the lay public. Life expectancy is estimated for national populations by most developed countries, including the United States, which has produced the estimate annually since 1945 and decennially since 1900. However, its calculation is relatively complex compared with that of other summary mortality measures, because it entails the calculation of six distinct functions and requires a minimum number of age groups and total population size, below\ which the estimates become unstable and unreliable." - USALEEP Methodology Summary The methodology used to calculate the U.S. censustract abridged life tables consisted of several stages. First, through a collaboration between the National Vital Statistics System registration areas and the National Center for Health Statistics, death records of U.S. residents (excluding residents of Maine and Wisconsin) for deaths occurring in 2010 through 2015 were geocoded using decedents’ residential addresses to identify and code census tracts. Second, population estimates were produced based on the 2010 decennial census and the 2011–2015 American Community Survey 5-year survey. Third, a methodology that combined standard demographic techniques and statistical modeling was developed to address challenges posed by small population sizes and small and missing age-specific death counts. Last, standard, abridged life table methods were adjusted to account for error introduced by population estimates based on sample data. To review the full methodology, please use the following link: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/series/sr_02/sr02_181.pdf
semantic_summary: This dataset provides small-area life expectancy estimates at birth for U.S. census tracts for the period 2010-2015. It includes life expectancy values, standard errors, and confidence intervals for specific census tracts, identified by neighborhood name, county, and state. Users can analyze health disparities by identifying which neighborhoods or census tracts had the highest or lowest life expectancy between 2010 and 2015.

description: This layer gives boundaried and grades of redlined areas in Denver. This layer can be overlaid with other current Denver data to illustrate how historical policies have influenced inequities in Denver today. REDLINING BACKGROUNDDenver, along with many other cities across the U.S., has a history of redlining. Government housing agencies assigned a grade from A to D to different neighborhoods in Denver and refused housing loans to people and families living in neighborhoods of a certain grade (namely grades C and D). Often, non-white populations lived in poor grade areas, and as a result, non-white families were not able to purchase homes. Home ownership is still one of the main ways to establish wealth in the United States and deeply rooted historical discriminatory policies, such as redlining, began a cycle of intergenerational poverty that still disproportionately impacts non-white populations today.For more information about the impacts of redlining, see the Undesign the Redline Exhibit website from Enterprise Community Foundation: http://www.designingthewe.com/undesign-the-redline

description: To support the business functions of the City and County of Denver Wastewater Management Division The FIRM is the basis for floodplain management, mitigation, and insurance activities for the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP). Insurance applications include enforcement of the mandatory purchase requirement of the Flood Disaster Protection Act, which "... requires the purchase of flood insurance by property owners who are being assisted by Federal programs or by Federally supervised, regulated or insured agencies or institutions in the acquisition or improvement of land facilities" (Section 2 (b) (4) of the Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973). In addition to the identification of Special Flood Hazard Areas (SFHAs), the risk zones shown on the FIRMs are the basis for the establishment of premium rates for flood coverage offered through the NFIP. The NFHL data present the flood risk information depicted on the FIRM in a digital format suitable for use in electronic mapping applications. The NFHL database is a subset of the information created for the FIS and serves as a means to archive a portion of the information collected during the FIS. The National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL) data incorporates all Digital Flood Insurance Rate Map(DFIRM) databases published by FEMA, and any Letters Of Map Revision (LOMRs) that have been issued against those databases since their publication date. The DFIRM Database is the digital, geospatial version of the flood hazard information shown on the published paper Flood Insurance Rate Maps(FIRMs). The primary risk classifications used are the 1-percent-annual-chance flood event, the 0.2-percent-annual-chance flood event, and areas of minimal flood risk. The NFHL data are derived from Flood Insurance Studies (FISs), previously published Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs), flood hazard analyses performed in support of the FISs and FIRMs, and new mapping data where available. The FISs and FIRMs are published by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). The specifications for the horizontal control of DFIRM data are consistent with those required for mapping at a scale of 1:12,000. The NFHL data contain layers in the Standard DFIRM datasets except for S_Label_Pt and S_Label_Ld. The NFHL is available as State or US Territory data sets. Each State or Territory data set consists of all DFIRMs and corresponding LOMRs available on the publication date of the data set.

description: This data set should be used for planning and analysis activities within the City and County of Denver to develop agency, department, or citywide indexes for the City and County of Denver. This data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a census. Results should be considered estimates and be used for high level planning purposes only.Since this data was internally derived by the City and County of Denver from census tract level data, Margin of Error statistics from the census tract data could not be accurately aggregated for the neighborhood level data. Therefore, the Margin of Error data is not provided with this data set. Users should use caution as data values are estimates.

description: Building roofprints delineated from 2022 aerial imagery. CAPTURE CRITERIA: Building roofprint polygons are stereocompiled in 3D. Outlines of permanent, visible structures are captured at the corners of the roof (eave). Buildings with area greater than or equal to 48 square feet and over 5 feet in height are collected. Arms and indentations must be 2.5 feet or greater to be captured. Canopies, carport covers, and sheds are included. For multi-level commercial and/or industrial buildings, each level is captured as a unique record if the building is greater than or equal to 1000 square feet and the multi-level roof levels are greater than or equal to 400 square feet in area and over 5 feet in height. Each polygon is a separate record. Polygons that are part of the same building have the same building ID. For pitched roofs, the highest point is used to determine the building height. The lowest point is the common lowest point if the building is multi-level. ATTRIBUTION: Unique ID, Height (feet), Ground Elevation (feet), Building Type (Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Medical, Public, Garage/Shed, Parking Structure, Tank, Foundation/Ruin, Miscellaneous). Building addresses are available for project partners, courtesy of BuildingFootprintsUSA. CHANGE FEATURES: This dataset is an update to previously collected data. Features were originally delineated from 2014 aerial imagery, updated in 2016, 2018, 2020, and then again in 2022 to create this dataset. Examples of change that are captured include but are not limited to: new features, change in attribution, and modifications that reach or exceed the threshold for initial collection of this feature. Additions refer not only to truly new features in the built environment but also to features that are added based on a larger extent of capture. Please refer to extent shapefiles for 2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, and 2022 feature captures before doing change analysis. Modifications are marked even if only a small portion of the feature has been changed. A separate change layer is available to show only those features that were delineated in 2022. SOURCE DATA: This feature was compiled from DRCOG 2022 Denver Regional Aerial Photography Project (DRAPP) imagery. This imagery is 4-band RGBIR color orthoimagery with a GSD (Ground Sample Distance) of 0.5 foot for 3-inch imagery, 1 foot for 6-inch imagery, and 2 feet for 12-inch imagery. Imagery was collected in the spring with a Vexcel Ultracam Eagle aerial sensor. Imagery is projected in the State Plane Coordinate System, Colorado Central Zone using the Lambert Conformal Conic map projection parameters. Horizontal and vertical datums are NAD83(11) and NAVD88(GEOID12A), respectively.

description: This dataset contains information regarding all HIV service providers that are currently funded by Part A of the Ryan White CARE Act. The Denver Office of HIV Resources distributes funding to these agencies to provide core and ancillary medical services to the HIV population in Adams, Aurora, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, and Jefferson counties. The ADAP Assistance site is also listed (administered by the Colorado Department of Health and the Environment) even though it is not funded by Part A. The Ryan White Part A CARE Grant operates on a fiscal year. The fiscal year begins every March 1st and ends on the last day of February. This dataset was created during FY 2011 and will be changed in future fiscal years only if any changes have taken place. About the Ryan White Care Act: The Ryan White Act is Federal legislation that addresses the unmet health needs of persons living with HIV (PLWH) by funding primary health care and support services. First passed by Congress in 1990 and reauthorized in 1996, 2000, 2006, and 2009. In 2009, the Act was extended until September 30, 2013. Programs are designed to improve the quality and availability of care for individuals and families affected by HIV disease in the United States and its territories. Ryan White Program Part A (Title I) funds provide emergency assistance to the urban areas most severely affected by the HIV epidemic. Part A funds include providers in the Denver Transitional Grant Area, which includes Adams, Arapahoe, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, and Jefferson counties. This data set contains the name, address, phone number, and website of each HIV health care provider that received Part A Ryan White CARE grant funds.

description: Displays local sector boundaries used for the RSP program. description: All Denver jurisdiction streets are made into routes for the Linear Referencing System by assigning LRS route names, and building routes by geoprocessing model. All public and private roads processed into routes. Dataset developed for transportation analysis within the City and County of Denver. The City and County of Denver's Street Route features constructed from the City's Street Centerline layer. Route geometry is the continuous street length until it stops at a "T" intersection or a street end. The route name contains "W" or a "S" for streets containing a West or South directional (respectively) within the street name. The routes are numbered and increase from Broadway - to the East and again to the West. Route numbering also begins at Elsworth - increasing to the North and again to the South

This resource is designed for transportation analysis, enabling users to identify and segment roads by their LRS route names for various linear referencing applications.

description: The purpose of this layer is to provide an accurate representation of impervious surfaces in the City and County of Denver. This layer combines Stormwater Billing impervious surfaces with planimetric impervious surfaces; allowing for a comprehensive, citywide, impervious surface layer. The purpose of this layer is to provide an accurate representation of impervious surfaces in the City and County of Denver. This layer combines Stormwater Billing impervious surfaces with Planimetric impervious surfaces; allowing for a comprehensive, city-wide, impervious surface layer. This layer is a compilation of two independent sources of impervious surface data. The data is provided by both the City and County of Denver’s Wastewater Management Division-Customer Service (WMD-CS) and Kucera International Inc. The WMD-CS data represents areas digitized for all stormwater billing inspections after December 2002 and contains impervious surface delineations of each inspected property. These features are updated daily by WMD-CS field investigators and GIS personnel. The planimetric data, supplied by Kucera International Inc, defines the stereocompiled features of the DRCOG Denver Region Urbanized Project Area. The features were compiled from the Denver Regional Aerial Photography Project (DRAPP) 2016/2018/2020 Aerial Imagery Acquisition and Production. This 1"=100' scale imagery is comprised of 4-band RGBIR color orthoimagery with a GSD (Ground Sample Distance) of 0.5'. Imagery was collected with the Leica ADS40 and ADS80 digital sensors and processed with Leica XPro software. Imagery is projected in State Plane Coordinate System, Colorado central zone using the Lambert Conformal Conic map projection parameters. Horizontal and vertical datums are NAD83(11) and NAVD88(GEOID12A) respectively. The planimetric features are generally updated every two years.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current impervious surface data for the City and County of Denver. It tracks impervious surface delineations, including details on `MEASUREMENT_DATE`, `IMPERVIOUS_TYPE`, and `SOURCE_DATA`. What is the total area of impervious surfaces in a specific Denver neighborhood, and what types of impervious surfaces are present?

This dataset provides current information on natural lake utility assets within the City of Denver. It details lake names, ownership, maintenance, lifecycle status, various water release and total volume measurements, regulatory water quality, and their associated water management and stormwater basin districts. Users can identify natural lake assets, inquire about their current ownership, water quality status, and hydrological capacities within specific water management districts.

This dataset provides current geographic information on natural streams located within the City of Denver. It details each bridge's unique identifier, category, ownership, build year, primary use, structural notes, geographical coordinates, reported issues, recommended projects, and estimated cost. This data can help users identify areas within a quarter-mile proximity to Denver parkland for urban planning, design, or cartographic purposes.

description: DPR Maintained Areas as of June 15, 2021
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies Denver Parks and Recreation (DPR) maintained areas as of June 15, 2021. It tracks specific park locations by formal name, type, class, GIS acreage, maintenance district, address, service level, and supervisor. Users can identify maintained areas, their service level, GIS acreage, and responsible supervisor within a specific park type or maintenance district.

description: Parks PSA data, updated June 24, 2025. This dataset is a polygon representation of parks and other areas maintained by the Department of Parks and Recreation in the City and County of Denver. This is not a comprehensive inventory of parkland or maintained areas; these are the primary locations of maintained areas.
semantic_summary: This dataset represents Denver's maintained park and plantable spaces as of June 2025. It tracks park locations, formal names, types, classes, GIS acres, maintenance districts, irrigation status, and associated neighborhood details. Users can query which maintained areas are irrigated, identify parks by type and class, or locate spaces within specific maintenance districts or neighborhoods.

This dataset contains official information on current parkland properties within the City and County of Denver. It tracks park location, formal name, type, class, acreage, acquisition date, master plan status, maintenance and council districts, available facilities, and detailed address and geographic coordinates. This data helps answer queries such as identifying designated parks by acreage, available facilities, or their administrative location within a specific council or police district.

This dataset describes Denver's general parkway network. It tracks key geographic details for each parkway segment, including its specific street name, total area, and linear length. Users can query this data to identify individual parkway segments by street name or calculate the total area and length of Denver's entire parkway system.

description: ARPA
semantic_summary: Current data on Denver's ARPA-funded program participation is available. It tracks the percentage of participants and the specific neighborhood associated with that participation. This data can answer questions like, "Which Denver neighborhoods have the highest or lowest percentage of participation in ARPA programs?"

description: Testing pavement super sectors
semantic_summary: This dataset outlines the ongoing pavement super sectors within the City of Denver. It tracks individual Super Sector IDs and their historical metadata, including creation and edit dates, and the responsible creators or editors. Users can query this data to determine when specific Super Sectors were created or last updated, and by whom.

description: Paving projects that may impact lining during 2024 and 2025
semantic_summary: This dataset details City of Denver paving projects scheduled for 2024 and 2025. It includes information such as affected street names, pavement classification, lane miles, planned work, mill and overlay statuses, asphalt types, and treatment strategies. Users can query this data to identify specific street segments impacted by paving, assess project completion dates, or analyze planned treatment methods and moratorium details.

This dataset details current and planned street paving projects across the City of Denver. It tracks project specifics including street names, maintenance jurisdiction, lane miles, committed and completion dates, treatment types, asphalt details, and current milling or overlay status. Users can identify active paving areas, determine a project's timeline or treatment specifications, or check for street moratoriums by specific location or status.

This dataset contains current City of Denver project field data collected across various municipal initiatives. It tracks geographic features as points, lines, and polygons, detailing each entry by its Project Name, Feature Description, and responsible Project Manager. Users can investigate which features belong to a specific Project Name or identify projects managed by a particular Project Manager.

This dataset details current pedestrian infrastructure projects and planning information for the City of Denver. It tracks project names, associated plans, asset classifications, and the current phase of each project, identified by unique DME and DOTI IDs. Users can query this data to identify all pedestrian projects associated with a specific plan, determine the current phase of an asset, or list projects by their asset classification.

This dataset details current and ongoing pedestrian improvement projects and planning for the City of Denver. It includes project names, improvement types, planned costs, status, length, and comprehensive scoring metrics such as equity, mobility, safety, sustainability, community connectivity, and overall prioritization rank. Users can identify highly prioritized pedestrian projects by their improvement type, estimated costs, and scores related to equity, safety, or overall rank.

This dataset details Denver's pedestrian infrastructure projects, reflecting current planning and status as of an August 2024 snapshot. It tracks attributes such as plan name, cost, project status, current phase, improvement type, priority, and various scoring metrics for mobility, safety, equity, and sustainability goals. Users can identify the status and estimated costs of pedestrian improvement projects, or assess projects based on their equity, safety, and community impact scores.

description: This data set should be used for planning and analysis of activities that are within the City and County of Denver. Neighborhood level data from the derived from the American Community Survey; 5 year average, years 2011-2015. Data was aggregated at the census tract level, and the summarized into neighborhoods. This information was then joined with Community Planning and Developments Neighborhoods layer. This data-set does not contain data for any enclaves administered by other jurisdictions that are located within the City and County of Denver's boundary. This data is a sample, not a census. Results should be considered estimates. Since this data was internally derived by the City and County of Denver from census tract level data, Margin of Error statistics from the census tract data could not be accurately aggregated for the neighborhood level data. Therefore, the Margin of Error data is not provided with this data set. Users should use caution as data values are estimates.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides neighborhood-level percent minority population estimates for Denver from the 2011-2015 American Community Survey. It tracks neighborhood names, district numbers, population density, the number and percentage of non-Hispanic White residents, and minority population counts. Use this data to analyze and compare minority population percentages and overall population density within different Denver neighborhoods for urban planning.

description: Feature layer generated from running the Create Buffers analysis tool.
semantic_summary: This dataset outlines current quarter-mile buffer zones for Denver's rail stations. It tracks details for each buffered area, including station name, transit line, operational status, number of parking spaces, opening year, typology, and the buffer's area in square miles. Users can identify the total area of buffers for operational stations, assess proximity to specific transit lines, or determine parking availability at stations within these zones.

description: Rebate Census Tracts
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies and defines geographic areas designated as Rebate Census Tracts for City of Denver programs. Each tract includes its unique tract number, an associated income qualification (IQ) metric, and a designated grant or rebate rate (GR). This data helps users identify which census tracts qualify for city rebate programs, allowing for analysis of areas based on income qualifications (IQ) and applicable rebate rates (GR).

description: Rebate Council District
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current geographic boundaries and associated information for City of Denver Rebate Council Districts. It tracks individual council district boundaries, along with attributes for Incentive Qualification (IQ) and Grant Rebate (GR) amounts. Users can query this data to determine specific rebate qualifications and grant rebate values available within each district number.

description: Rebate Neighborhood
semantic_summary: This dataset details Denver's current neighborhood-based rebate programs. It identifies each Neighborhood Name and tracks associated GR and IQ metrics. Users can analyze which neighborhoods are involved in rebate programs and compare their GR and IQ values.

This dataset details Denver's recreation center branch service areas as of 2023. It tracks the geographic extent of each service area, including square mileage, and provides detailed information for each associated recreation center such as branch name, address, phone, hours, year built, building square footage, marketed facilities, and program links. Users can identify the service area and associated recreation center details, such as address, operating hours, and available programs, for any location in Denver.

description: Overlap between bike facilities and parks
semantic_summary: This dataset details Denver's existing and planned bike facilities, specifically highlighting their overlap with park boundaries. It tracks attributes like bikeway names, length in miles, installation or plan years, funding sources, and mechanism, alongside park names, types, acreage, and included facilities. Users can query to identify recommended bikeway lengths or planned installation years for new facilities intersecting specific park types or council districts.

description: ARPA
semantic_summary: This dataset tracks Denver's community recovery efforts related to the American Rescue Plan Act. It details various facets of recovery through indices measuring economic, health, and education outcomes, along with a comprehensive full recovery index. Users can analyze which areas in Denver show the most or least progress across economic, health, and education recovery indices.

description: Redline
semantic_summary: This dataset details historical residential security assessments, commonly known as redlining, from 1938. It tracks detailed and general residential security grades, their descriptions, overlay information, and associated notes for specific indexed areas. Users can analyze how residential areas were graded and described in 1938, and identify the notes and overlays for specific locations.

description: Regional Control Measures_Regional_ControlMeasures
semantic_summary: This dataset documents current and ongoing regional control measures and associated infrastructure. The data tracks facility details such as unique IDs, ownership, maintenance status, installation dates, associated lake names, water quality impacts, release volumes, and regulatory compliance. Users can identify control measure facilities by owner, total release volume, or water quality impact within specific stream sub-basins.

This dataset provides current regional administrative boundaries and associated public health statistics. It tracks administrative boundaries for counties and municipalities, and provides public health statistics including confirmed cases, negative cases, total tests, recovered cases, deaths, and pending tests by county. Users can determine current public health statistics for a specific county or analyze the spatial distribution of cases and deaths across regional administrative areas.

description: Feature layer generated from running the Create Buffers analysis tool.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current spatial analysis of residential buffers and associated zoning information for the City of Denver. It tracks key details such as zone description, zone district, neighborhood context, zone use function, buffer distance in miles, and the calculated area in square miles for buffered features. Users can query this data to understand zoning regulations, neighborhood context, or the area of specific zone districts within defined buffer distances around residential properties.

description: Feature layer generated from running the Create Buffers analysis tool.
semantic_summary: This feature layer delineates current residential buffer zones across the City of Denver. It tracks buffered features, detailing each zone's specific buffer distance in feet and its corresponding area in square miles. Users can query this data to determine the area covered by residential buffers at various distances.

description: Feature layer generated from running the Create Buffers analysis tool.
semantic_summary: This dataset details current 300-foot geographic buffers around residential properties. It includes attributes for the specific buffer distance in feet and the calculated area in square miles for each buffered feature. This data helps users answer questions like "What is the total area in square miles within a particular 300-foot residential buffer?"

This dataset maps the City of Denver's residential zone districts as of June 2024. It includes details such as zoning code versions, district descriptions, neighborhood context, and permitted zone use functions. Users can identify a specific zone district's description or determine the permitted uses within a particular neighborhood context.

description: Residential Parking Permit Streets
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies existing Residential Parking Permit Streets in the City of Denver. It tracks individual street segments by name, type, and full address range, along with associated attributes like speed limit, one-way status, and applicable ZIP codes. Users can identify specific streets requiring a residential parking permit and query details such as street name, address ranges, and hundred block information.

description: Streets with residential parking permits
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies current streets designated with residential parking permits across the City of Denver. It tracks individual street names and their corresponding Residential Parking Permit (RPP) zone designations. Users can quickly find out if a street requires a permit and determine its specific RPP name.

fields.name: Drink_Included_In_Kids_Meal
fields.alias: Drink Included In Kids Meal Price

semantic_summary: This dataset contains current information on Denver restaurants and their kids' meal options. It details restaurant name, address, business type, if kids' meals are found online, chain status, and specific drink options such as soda, 100% juice, and flavored milk, noting if a drink is included in the meal price. This data allows users to find Denver restaurants with kids' meals, compare available drink choices like soda versus 100% juice, and check if drinks are part of the kids' meal price.

This dataset provides current information on active retail gas stations. It details each facility's name, type, category, original ID, current tank status, number of active tanks, and full address with geographic coordinates. Users can identify the location, operational status, and number of active tanks for specific gas stations or within defined geographic regions.

description: Riparian Buffer for HRCS outline only
semantic_summary: This dataset defines current riparian buffers, specifically for the HRCS outline. The data tracks the linear extent of each designated riparian buffer. Users can query the linear length of specific riparian buffers within the HRCS outline to understand their spatial extent.

description: To show parcels within the City and County of Denver that intersect with the Healthy River Corridor proposed 50' South Platte River buffer.
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies parcels within the City and County of Denver that intersect with the proposed 50-foot South Platte River buffer. It includes details such as parcel identification numbers, owner names and addresses, situs addresses, property class, zoning, and appraised and assessed property values. Users can identify property owners, their addresses, and key property characteristics like zoning and assessed values for parcels located within the proposed river buffer zone.

This dataset maps 2023 branch service areas associated with Registered Neighborhood Organizations (RNOs) in Denver. It includes details like RNO names, comprehensive contact information, membership numbers, and the calculated area and length of their geographic boundaries. This data allows users to identify specific RNOs by name, find contact persons, determine membership counts, and analyze the spatial extent of service areas.

This dataset provides ongoing tracking of reported road debris incidents. It captures specific debris types along with precise geographic coordinates, altitude, speed, direction of travel, and detailed GPS accuracy metrics at the time of capture. This data helps users pinpoint debris locations, analyze reporting trends over time, and understand the context and reliability of each incident.

description: PSA data for public ROW. Updated 11/4/2025
semantic_summary: This dataset details the current analysis of plantable spaces within Denver's public Right-of-Way, with an update scheduled for November 4, 2025. It describes plantable space classifications and neighborhood context, linking them to specific neighborhood names and referencing CDOT-related information. Users can query which neighborhoods contain specific types of plantable spaces and their contextual information within the public Right-of-Way.

This dataset details current Right-of-Way Enforcement Focus Areas within the City of Denver. It tracks geographic focus areas by district and beat numbers, street names, along with details like enforcement hours and days for time marking and Residential Parking Permits (RPP), meters, and safety notes. Users can query to identify Right-of-Way enforcement zones, their associated time marking and RPP enforcement hours and days, or specific safety concerns within designated focus areas.

description: Residential Parking Permit streets
semantic_summary: This dataset identifies current Residential Parking Permit (RPP) street segments throughout the City of Denver. It includes details such as street name, 'from' and 'to' street names defining segments, and counts of active, pending, and issued permits for each segment. Users can query which streets are designated RPP zones and determine the number of active, pending, or issued residential parking permits on specific street segments.

This dataset outlines current Restricted Special Areas (RSAs) for the City of Denver. It tracks the geographic extent, descriptive details, and current phase of each designated area. Users can identify the purpose and status of specific RSAs or analyze the total area by phase.

description: This layer contains all RTD bus stops within a 10 minute walk distance from DPL locations
semantic_summary: Current RTD bus stops are mapped within a 10-minute walk of Denver Public Library locations. This layer details bus stop IDs, names, routes, and geographic coordinates, along with the distance to specific DPL branches including their names and addresses. This data helps users find accessible bus stops for DPL branches, explore service routes, and determine walking distances to library facilities.

description: SA_ATO23
semantic_summary: This dataset provides a 2023 cumulative score for access to opportunity within the City and County of Denver. It tracks various individual and composite scores covering regular, commercial, location, and transit access, alongside equity dimensions like social, healthcare, morbidity, mortality, and built environment, often with food access, park access, poverty, and education metrics by neighborhood. This data allows users to analyze which neighborhoods face the greatest disparities in access to care, healthy food, parks, or education, and to identify areas requiring targeted interventions.

fields.name: Estimate__Median_household_inco
fields.alias: Estimate!!Median household income in the past 12 months (in 2018 inflation-adjusted dollars)

semantic_summary: This dataset contains 2020 socio-economic and housing equity analysis data for Denver. It tracks various community well-being indicators including overall Equity Score, average access scores, housing diversity scores, median household income, educational attainment, and housing tenure percentages. This data can answer questions such as which Denver neighborhoods exhibit the highest or lowest Equity Scores, access to care, educational attainment, or median household income.

This dataset identifies current geographic areas within Denver designated for safety focus. It tracks the unique names of these areas and their geometric length. Users can query this data to find out the names and perimeters of designated safety focus areas across the city.

description: Sales and Use tax amounts and YoY change % by Neighborhood

layers.name: Sales and Use Tax Collected In each Neighborhood

semantic_summary: This dataset details annual sales and use tax collected by Denver neighborhoods from 2017 to 2021. It tracks total sales and use tax collected per neighborhood annually, along with year-over-year percentage changes and an overall change from 2017-2021. How have sales and use tax collections changed for specific Denver neighborhoods between 2017 and 2021, and which areas experienced the largest percentage growth or decline?

description: Salesforce_All_In
semantic_summary: This dataset contains current operational data on City of Denver Salesforce cases and associated "House1000Sites" information. It tracks City of Denver Salesforce cases with attributes like case status, resolution, incident address, and assigned agency, along with House1000Sites details including address, ownership, operational status, and bed capacity. This data can answer questions such as "What is the operational status and bed capacity of 'House1000Sites' within a specific district, and how many active Salesforce cases are associated with these locations?"

description: Salesforce_All_In_Buffer_Geodesic
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current operational and planning details for specific sites within Denver's micro-communities. It tracks attributes such as site address, potential use, district, ownership, acreage, development status, number of units and beds, and community meeting dates for each location. Users can query this data to identify sites by potential use or district, determine operational status and capacity (units/beds), or find upcoming community meeting dates.

description: Sanitary pipes for the 2025 Pipe Rehabilitation Phase 1, FFP City and County of Denver Wastewater Management Sanitary Facility Data - Sanitary Sewer Mains.
semantic_summary: This dataset covers Denver's 2025 Phase 1 sanitary sewer pipe rehabilitation lining project. It tracks details for individual rehabilitated sanitary sewer mains including facility ID, pipe diameter, pipe length, pipe type, lining type, and lining date. Users can query which specific pipes, identified by facility ID and length, are scheduled for which lining type and date within this rehabilitation phase.

description: SAVTD_21
semantic_summary: This dataset details the vulnerability to displacement for the year 2021. It includes indicators such as neighborhood names, GEOID tracts, educational attainment percentages, renter and owner occupancy rates, median household income, and various vulnerability scores. This data helps identify neighborhoods with high total displacement vulnerability, analyze the relationship between income and education, or understand housing tenure by area.

This dataset tracks the usage of SCA reference forms over various years. It records form usage details including the year, associated postal code, and country code for each entry. Users can analyze annual usage trends by geographical areas or determine which postal codes show the highest form usage per year.

This dataset provides current and historical location and operational data for schools within the City of Denver. It details school names, types, grade levels, addresses, websites, enrollment figures, and various operational metrics including traffic safety, equity area status, and potential capacity. Users can analyze school distribution, resource allocation, and identify specific facilities by school type, grade level, and enrollment to assess community needs or transportation planning.

This dataset delineates 2023 school service areas linked to city branches. It includes detailed attributes for each service area, such as school names, districts, types, grade levels, and the associated branch names, regions, and addresses, along with the area in square miles. It helps users determine which schools are served by specific city branches and analyze the geographic coverage of these service areas.

description: ARPA
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current Denver community well-being index scores. It tracks comprehensive full index scores, along with specific indices for health, education, and economic well-being across Denver. Users can analyze this data to identify Denver communities with the greatest need based on their Health, Education, Economic, and Full Index scores for targeted interventions.

This dataset identifies significant flooding locations across Denver during 2019. This data tracks the specific geographic points where significant flooding incidents were officially recorded. This dataset helps users identify specific locations impacted by significant flooding in 2019 and analyze the spatial distribution of these events for planning.

This dataset details proposed storm routing segments for the City of Denver, categorized by SDMP Study Year. It tracks infrastructure characteristics such as conduit shape, horizontal and vertical sizes, barrel count, alongside associated proposed project letters, names, and descriptions. Users can identify proposed storm infrastructure by project name or letter and query its physical dimensions (H-Size, V-Size) for specific study years.

description: Master layer of Site Development Plans and concepts for use in Dashboard.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides current and ongoing Site Development Plans and concepts for the City of Denver. It includes details for each plan such as Record ID, Record Type, Application Name, Opened Date, Full Address, and the associated Project Coordination District. Users can utilize this data to search for specific development plans by address, identify application types, review opening dates, or locate projects within a given district.

description: SDP or Concept Case 7 - No need to filter, not entire dataset
semantic_summary: This dataset tracks Site Development Plan (SDP) and concept cases in Denver from September 2021 to March 2022. It tracks key details such as record IDs, application names, case types, current status and dates, descriptions, and full addresses associated with each development or concept case. Users can query this data to find the status of a specific site development plan, understand application descriptions by address, or identify all cases opened within a particular timeframe.

description: SDP or Concept Case 9 - Sept 2022 - Feb 2023
semantic_summary: This dataset tracks Site Development Plans (SDPs) and Concept Cases submitted to the City of Denver from September 2022 to February 2023. It includes details such as the application's record ID, type, current status and date, application name, description, opened date, and full address of the proposed development. Users can query to find all active development plans at a specific address, track the status of a particular record ID, or view proposed applications opened within this period.

description: SDP and Concept Records - September 2018 - August 2021
semantic_summary: This dataset contains SDP and Concept Records for the City of Denver, covering the period from September 2018 through August 2021. It details each record's type, current status, application name, description, and various dates including when it was opened, linked to specific street addresses. This data can answer questions about the status of specific records, the types of applications active or expired, or all related records associated with a particular street address.

description: SDPs_Concepts_Mar2022_Aug2022
semantic_summary: This dataset details Denver's Site Development Plans and related concepts from March to August 2022. It tracks individual records by their ID, type, and current status, along with application names, descriptions, opened dates, and full address information. Users can query to find all Site Development Plans opened within a specific date range, their current status, or the address associated with a particular record type.

description: Select marijuana stores for EXL request Spring 25
semantic_summary: This dataset details selected marijuana store locations for Spring 2025. It includes attributes such as location name, status, geocoded address, X/Y coordinates, and matching quality scores for each entry. Users can easily identify the precise geocoded location, address, and status of selected marijuana stores within Denver.

description: 1k foot buffer of select marijuana stores for EXL request Spring 25
semantic_summary: Spring 2025 marijuana store buffers define geographic zones around selected cannabis dispensaries. This dataset tracks the specific location, address, and buffer distance for each designated area. Users can identify which addresses and areas are impacted by a 1,000-foot proximity to select marijuana stores.

This dataset contains current administrative records detailing division sign-offs for park-related initiatives. It tracks specific park names, relevant meeting dates, attending divisions, associated notes, and links for tracking comments. Users can identify which divisions attended sign-off meetings for specific park projects, along with relevant meeting dates and comment tracking information.

semantic_summary: This dataset comprises current applicability forms for stormwater and flood control projects submitted to Denver's DOTI. It tracks project area conditions like imperviousness and floodplain status, on-site treatment percentages, selected standards (WQCV, Pollutant Removal, Runoff Reduction), and details on regional or non-regional off-site control measures, including their receiving waters and facility IDs. Users can query this data to assess projects' compliance with stormwater treatment standards, determine treated impervious areas, and identify connections between projects, HUC10 watersheds, and specific control measure facilities.

description: Social Vulnerability Index Denver 2022 - CDC/ATSDR The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry Social Vulnerability Index (hereafter, CDC/ATSDR SVI or SVI) is a place-based index, database, and mapping application designed to identify and quantify communities experiencing social vulnerability. The Geospatial Research, Analysis & Services Program (GRASP) maintains the CDC/ATSDR SVI to help public health officials and local planners better prepare for and respond to emergency events with the goal of decreasing human suffering, economic loss, and health inequities. The current CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index uses 16 U.S. census variables from the 5-year American Community Survey (ACS) to identify communities that may need support before, during, or after disasters. These variables are grouped into four themes that cover four major areas of social vulnerability and then combined into a single measure of overall social vulnerability. For more information visit CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index . For data and column information visit CDC/ATSDR SVI 2022 Documentation
semantic_summary: This dataset provides the 2022 CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index for communities within the City of Denver. It quantifies social vulnerability based on 16 census variables, tracking estimated population, poverty rates, unemployment, education, age, disability, minority status, and access to vehicles. Users can identify Denver neighborhoods with the highest overall social vulnerability or specific issues like high poverty or lack of vehicle access for targeted resource allocation.

description: This scene shows 3D buildings for STRIVE Prep - RISE/DSST Green Valley Ranch Campus with a shadow frequency raster overlaid on the buidlings for ground level and rooftop shadows. Building roofprints delineated from 2018 aerial imagery. CAPTURE CRITERIA: Building roofprint polygons are stereocompiled in 3D. Outlines of permanent, visible structures are captured at the corners of the roof (eave). Buildings with area greater than or equal to 48 square feet and over 5 feet in height are collected. Arms and indentations must be 2.5 feet or greater to be captured. Canopies, carport covers, and sheds are included. For multi-level commercial and/or industrial buildings, each level is captured as a unique record if the building is greater than or equal to 1000 square feet and the multi-level roof levels are greater than or equal to 400 square feet in area and over 5 feet in height. Each polygon is a separate record. Polygons that are part of the same building have the same building ID. For pitched roofs, the highest point is used to determine the building height. The lowest point is the common lowest point if the building is multi-level. ATTRIBUTION: Unique ID, Height (feet), Ground Elevation (feet), Building Type (Residential, Commercial, Industrial, Medical, Public, Garage/Shed, Parking Structure, Tank, Foundation/Ruin, Miscellaneous). Building addresses are available for project partners, courtesy of BuildingFootprintsUSA. CHANGE FEATURES: This dataset is an update to previously collected data. Features were originally delineated from 2014 aerial imagery, updated in 2016, and then again in 2018 to create this dataset. Examples of change that are captured include but are not limited to: new features, change in attribution, and modifications that reach or exceed the threshold for initial collection of this feature. Additions refer not only to truly new features in the built environment but also to features that are added based on a larger extent of capture. Please refer to extent shapefiles for 2014, 2016 and 2018 feature captures before doing change analysis. Modifications are marked even if only a small portion of the feature has been changed. A separate change layer is available to show only those features that were delineated in 2018. SOURCE DATA: This feature was compiled from DRCOG 2018 Denver Regional Aerial Photography Project (DRAPP) imagery. This imagery is 4-band RGBIR color orthoimagery with a GSD (Ground Sample Distance) of 0.5 foot for 3-inch imagery, 1 foot for 6-inch imagery, and 2 feet for 12-inch imagery. Imagery was collected in the spring with a Vexcel Ultracam Eagle aerial sensor. Imagery is projected in the State Plane Coordinate System, Colorado Central Zone using the Lambert Conformal Conic map projection parameters. Horizontal and vertical datums are NAD83(11) and NAVD88(GEOID12A), respectively.

description: Produced and Published by Colorado Division of Oil and Public Safety DDPHE Data Steward: Andrew Ross Each point represents a Regulated Storage tank and attached release information (if any). The dataset was created by the following data sources are joined by Facility ID. Regulated Storage Tank Facilities in Colorado, Oil & Public Safety | Colorado Information Marketplace | data.colorado.gov This dataset includes information about storage tanks registered with the State of Colorado, Department of Labor & Employment, Division of Oil & Public Safety. The data are a combination of information provided by the owner and collected during inspection by the State of Colorado, Department of Labor & Employment, Division of Oil & Public Safety. There is no guarantee the data published are 100% accurate, correct, current or complete. This dataset does not include tanks that were applied for installation permit but were denied or never installed. The This information is also publically accessible at https://opus.cdle.state.co.us/OIS2000/ Facilities with no tank count may be associated with Release Events or no tank information is available. Count of Tanks includes all in-use and closed tanks. Tanks that applied for installation, but were not installed are not included. Some address fields are descriptions of location where there is no mailing address, or no address was provided. Updated Monthly. Petroleum Releases, Colorado Oil & Public Safety | Colorado Information Marketplace | data.colorado.gov This dataset includes information about Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) system and Underground Storage Tank (UST) system petroleum release events, with their associated locations, contacts for remediation, and status in relation to currently being investigated, assessed, remediated, obtaining closure, or closed, dating back to 1986. The data are provided by the State of Colorado, Department of Labor & Employment, Division of Oil & Public Safety. There is no guarantee the data published are 100% accurate, correct, current or complete. This information is also publicly accessible at https://opus.cdle.state.co.us/OIS2000/ Tiered Closures: Tier I risk-based screening levels (RBSLs) are the default maximum concentrations for chemicals of concern (COCs) used to determine whether remediation (cleanup) is required. Tier I closure types generally represent situations where contamination was at or below the Tier I RBSLs at assessment or after remediation efforts have been completed. Tier II site-specific target level(s) (SSTLs) are the risk-based remedial action target levels for COCs developed for a particular site using site-specific geological and hydrogeological data in a predictive model. Tier II closure types generally represent situations where contaminants may be present on site, but pose no risk to the known points of exposure. Tier III closure criteria establishes conditions where all exposure pathways have been eliminated, even though dissolved-phase COCs remain above Tier I RBSLs beyond the release property boundary and beneath, but not beyond the adjoining public roadway. Tier IV closure criteria establishes conditions where all exposure pathways have been eliminated, even though dissolved-phase COCs remain above Tier I RBSLs beyond the release property boundary irrespective of land use and where no storage tanks remain on the release property. Release Events without a release date may represent records of tank closure assessment with no indication of contamination or COCs below Tier 1 RBSLs, a phase 2 Environmental Site Assessment with no indication of contamination or concentrations below Tier 1 screening levels, a Brownfield redevelopment site, and/or a release Event that pre-dates the use of release date records. Generally, lower Event ID numbers represent older release discoveries and higher Event ID numbers represent more recent release discoveries. Reimbursement amounts of zero imply that an application for reimbursement has been submitted and approved, but no costs have been reimbursed. Blank cells imply that the Event has not applied for reimbursement of remediation costs. Negative amounts imply that the required deductible amount has not yet been met. Updated Monthly.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides historical and current information on regulated storage tank facilities and associated petroleum release events across Colorado. It tracks facility details, active and closed tank counts, geographical locations, and comprehensive release event data including dates, causes, statuses, and specific closure types (Tier I-IV), along with contact information. Users can identify facilities with regulated storage tanks, determine the status and closure type of petroleum release events, or locate contact information for remediation.

description: This layer contains the most current release of data from the American Community Survey (ACS) about median household income by race and by age of householder. These are 5-year estimates by the U.S. Census Bureau filtered by Denver County Published by DDPHE/SSBO Data Steward: Roxanne Eidom Although the American Community Survey (ACS) produces population, demographic and housing unit estimates, the decennial census is the official source of population totals for April 1st of each decennial year. In between censuses, the Census Bureau's Population Estimates Program produces and disseminates the official estimates of the population for the nation, states, counties, cities, and towns and estimates of housing units for states and counties. Information about the American Community Survey (ACS) can be found on the ACS Website . Supporting documentation including code lists, subject definitions, data accuracy, and statistical testing, and a full list of ACS tables and table shells (without estimates) can be found on the Technical Documentation section of the ACS website. Sample size and data quality measures (including coverage rates, allocation rates, and response rates) can be found on the American Community Survey website in the Methodology section. Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2019-2023 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates. Data are based on a sample and are subject to sampling variability. The degree of uncertainty for an estimate arising from sampling variability is represented through the use of a margin of error. The value shown here is the 90 percent margin of error. The margin of error can be interpreted roughly as providing a 90 percent probability that the interval defined by the estimate minus the margin of error and the estimate plus the margin of error (the lower and upper confidence bounds) contains the true value. In addition to sampling variability, the ACS estimates are subject to nonsampling error (for a discussion of nonsampling variability, see ACS Technical Documentation . The effect of nonsampling error is not represented in these tables. The 2019-2023 American Community Survey (ACS) data generally reflect the March 2020 Office of Management and Budget (OMB) delineations of metropolitan and micropolitan statistical areas. In certain instances, the names, codes, and boundaries of the principal cities shown in ACS tables may differ from the OMB delineation lists due to differences in the effective dates of the geographic entities. Estimates of urban and rural populations, housing units, and characteristics reflect boundaries of urban areas defined based on 2020 Census data. As a result, data for urban and rural areas from the ACS do not necessarily reflect the results of ongoing urbanization. Explanation of Symbols: The estimate could not be computed because there were an insufficient number of sample observations. For a ratio of medians estimate, one or both of the median estimates falls in the lowest interval or highest interval of an open-ended distribution. For a 5-year median estimate, the margin of error associated with a median was larger than the median itself. The estimate or margin of error cannot be displayed because there were an insufficient number of sample cases in the selected geographic area. The estimate or margin of error is not applicable or not available. The median falls in the lowest interval of an open-ended distribution (for example \"2,500-\"). The median falls in the highest interval of an open-ended distribution (for example \"250,000+\").The margin of error could not be computed because there were an insufficient number of sample observations. The margin of error could not be computed because the median falls in the lowest interval or highest interval of an open-ended distribution. A margin of error is not appropriate because the corresponding estimate is controlled to an independent population or housing estimate. Effectively, the corresponding estimate has no sampling error and the margin of error may be treated as zero. This layer represents a moment in time and will not be updated. 5-year estimates are published as they are available through the ACS. Published February 2025. Data quality good.

It tracks over twenty health measures including total population, disability rates, chronic diseases like diabetes and asthma, mental distress, and health behaviors such as smoking, binge drinking, and physical activity among adults. Users can explore which Denver neighborhoods have higher or lower rates of conditions like obesity, diabetes, chronic disease, or frequent mental distress among adults.

This dataset provides current City of Denver development application records. It tracks essential details such as application type, status, filing dates, geographic location by address and neighborhood, and associated project manager contacts. Users can identify active applications, track specific record statuses, or find project manager information for development projects across Denver neighborhoods.

This dataset provides current and historical information on the City of Denver's sanitary sewer infrastructure. It tracks various components, including manholes, pipes, service lines, fittings, and structures, detailing their physical characteristics, ownership, maintenance, condition, installation dates, and project history across different drainage basins. Users can identify the location and dimensions of sanitary mains, assess the condition of manholes, or find the owner and maintenance history of specific service lines within a water management district.

description: Business Improvement Districts (BID) are allowed to acquire, construct, finance, install, and operate improvements including streets, sidewalks, curbs, gutters, pedestrian malls, streetlights, utilities, drainage facilities, landscaping, decorative structures, statuaries, fountains, identification signs, traffic safety devices, bicycle paths, off-street parking facilities, benches, rest rooms, information booths, public meeting facilities, and all necessary appurtenances. An organizational petition shall be signed by persons who own real or personal property in the service areaof the district having an assessed value of not less than 50% of the assessed value of all real and personal property in the district, and who own at least 50% of the acreage in the district as filed in the City Clerk and City Council offices.City Council approves the petition by ordinance, organizing the BID and defining the boundaries
semantic_summary: This dataset contains current and historical geographic boundaries for Denver's Business Improvement Districts (BIDs). Data includes district names, creation ordinances, legal start and end dates, boundary modification dates, and active or historical status for each district. This resource helps answer questions like "Which BIDs are currently active?", "What is the name and creation ordinance for a specific BID?", or "When were a district's boundaries last modified?".

description: This data is used by the Building Inspection Division to determine various inspection boundaries for permitting purposes. GIS data layers are accessed by personnel in most City departments for basic applications such as viewing, querying, and map output production. This map data layer represents the building inspection boundaries for construction inspections for the City and County of Denver, Colorado. The building inspection boundaries data layer is changed only when a inspection boundary and/or inspector assigned to a particular district has changed.
semantic_summary: This dataset details current building construction inspection boundaries for the City and County of Denver. It tracks inspection types, district numbers, assigned inspectors and chief inspectors with their contact information, and relevant dates and notes. Users can determine which inspector and inspection type apply to a specific construction district and retrieve their contact details.

description: This resource was developed to identify areas of responsibility for the Denver Department of Transportation and Infrastructure Office of Community and Business Engagement (OCBE). This layer uses City Council District boundraries to create areas of responsibility for the OCBE City Building Team. There are four (4) total areas: Area 1: City Council Districts 1 and 9 Area 2: City Council Districts 5, 8, and 11 Area 3: City Council Districts 2, 3, and 7 Area 4: City Council Districts 4, 6, 10
semantic_summary: This dataset defines the current areas of responsibility for the Denver Department of Transportation and Infrastructure Office of Community and Business Engagement (OCBE) City Building Team. It tracks four distinct responsibility areas, identifying the specific City Council Districts, assigned CBT Area Number, CBT Chairperson, and their contact information for each. Users can easily determine which City Council Districts fall under a specific OCBE City Building Team Area and who the responsible Chairperson is.

description: Dataset developed for determination of feature locations, names and for approved analytical purposes. The Department of Public Works of the City and County of Denver performs many functions including Construction Engineering Inspection. This geographic dataset represents the Construction Engineering Inspection Districts.
semantic_summary: This dataset represents the current administrative boundaries for Denver's Construction Engineering Inspection Districts. It tracks the geographic extent of each district along with detailed contact information for assigned personnel, including engineering supervisors, chief inspectors, area inspectors, mainline inspectors, and water/wastewater plumbers. Users can query this data to identify the responsible inspection personnel for a specific district, including their names, phone numbers, and email addresses.

description: To determine the development review person for a geographic area. ADMN_DEVREVIEW_A Geographic boundaries created to assign staff for the review of development plans.
semantic_summary: This dataset defines current administrative geographic boundaries for development review staff assignments within the City of Denver. It tracks the assigned project manager, their contact phone and email, and any relevant notes for each specific geographic area. Users can quickly identify the development review project manager, their phone number, or email for any given geographic area.

description: This data is used by the Building Inspection Division to determine various inspection boundaries for permitting purposes. This map data layer represents the building inspection boundaries for electrical inspections for the City and County of Denver, Colorado. The building inspection boundaries data layer is changed only when a inspection boundary and/or inspector assigned to a particular district has changed.
semantic_summary: This dataset outlines current electrical inspection boundaries for building permits in the City and County of Denver. It tracks inspection types, district numbers, chief and individual inspector names and contact information, and update dates. description: Metropolitan districts are the most common form of special districts that may be organized under C.R.S. Title 32 to provide ambulance services, fire protection, hospital, mosquito control, park and recreation, safety protection,(i.e., traffic and safety controls and devices on streets and highways), sanitation, street improvements, television relay and translation, transportation, and water development. Metro Districts are formed by:1. Approval by City Council of the district's service plan, which is the document that governs the district's actions;2. A petition signed by 30% or 200 of the electors of the District, whichever is less is approved by the District court and an election is ordered; and3. Approval of the District by the electors within the District.Subareas within the District may be formed.C. Governance.A metropolitan district is governed by a five member board of directors. A director must be an "elector" of such district, defined as a person who, at the time, is registered to vote in the State and: (I) who has been a resident of the district for not less than thirty days; or (II) who, or whose spouse, owns taxable real or personal property situated within the boundaries of the district, whether said person resides within the district or not. There is no City appointment. The board is responsible for the administration of the district, annual budgeting and levying of taxes,rates, and charges sufficient to pay operating costs and debt service of the district.D. Powers.1. Common Powers. All special districts have the following powers:a. To have a perpetual existence;b. To have and use a corporate seal;c. To sue and be sued;d. To enter into contracts and agreements affecting the affairs of the special district;e. To borrow money and incur indebtedness and to issue notes or issue bonds evidencing suchindebtedness;f. To acquire, sell and lease property;g. To manage, control and supervise all the business and affairs of the special district, including allconstruction, operation and maintenance of special district improvements;h. To fix, charge and collect fees, rates, tolls, penalties or charges for services, programs or facilitiesfurnished by the special district.i. To furnish services and facilities outside the boundaries of the special district.j. To adopt, amend, and enforce bylaws and rules and regulations for carrying on the business, objectsand affairs of the special district.2. Additional Powers Depending Upon Type of District:a. Metropolitan Districts: In addition to the common powers, metropolitan districts have the following powers: to enter into contracts with public utilities and municipalities for street lighting service;to erect and maintain traffic and safety controls and devices, providing fire protection, parks or recreation, water or water and sanitation service;

description: This dataset estimates the demand for walking in different areas of the City and County of Denver based on population and employment density. An estimate of the demand for walking in different areas of the City and County of Denver based on two data variables known to contribute to high levels of walking: population density and employment density. Population density (population per square mile) is sourced from the 2020 Census. Employment density (employment per square mile) is sourced from the Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics (LEHD) Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES) Version 7. Population and employment density are added together to generate a combined density value. This combined value is grouped into 10 value groupings using the Quantile method in ArcGIS. The 10 value groupings are then assigned a Pedestrian Demand Index Score (1 – 10), which is displayed by Traffic Analysis Zone. The higher the score, the higher the estimated demand for walking. Note: Due to geographic problems inherent in the 2010 Census block group data, used as the base geographic unit to combine employment and population data, results should be considered estimates.
semantic_summary: This dataset estimates the demand for walking in different areas of Denver, primarily based on 2020 Census population and employment data. It tracks a Pedestrian Demand Index Score (PDI_Score) and PDI_Ranking, derived from combining population and employment densities for Traffic Analysis Zones. This data helps identify which Denver areas have the highest estimated demand for walking, using the PDI_Score.

description: This dataset includes criminal offenses in the City and County of Denver for the previous five calendar years plus the current year to date. The data is based on the National Incident Based Reporting System (NIBRS) which includes all victims of person crimes and all crimes within an incident. The data is dynamic, which allows for additions, deletions and/or modifications at any time, resulting in more accurate information in the database. Due to continuous data entry, the number of records in subsequent extractions are subject to change. Crime data is updated Monday through Friday. The Denver Police Department strives to make crime data as accurate as possible, but there is no avoiding the introduction of errors into this process, which relies on data furnished by many people and that cannot always be verified. Data on this site are updated Monday through Friday, adding new incidents and updating existing data with information gathered through the investigative process.Not surprisingly, crime data become more accurate over time, as new incidents are reported and more information comes to light during investigations.Crimes that occurred at least 30 days ago tend to be the most accurate, although records are returned for incidents that happened yesterday. This dynamic nature of crime data means that content provided here today will probably differ from content provided a week from now. Likewise, content provided on this site will probably differ somewhat from crime statistics published elsewhere by the City and County of Denver, even though they draw from the same database.
semantic_summary: This dataset provides dynamic criminal offense records for the City and County of Denver, covering the past five full calendar years and the current year to date. description: Landscape Typology is a rapid functional assessment designed to delineate vegetation communities within parks owned and maintained by Denver Parks and Recreation (DPR) based on their vegetation structure and composition and assign a functional score based on a set of qualitative and semi-quantitative parameters. This database should be used as a reference to locate parks and identify their landscape types, subtypes, and function. Users can dive deeper into the dataset to determine dominant vegetation species and parameter scoring to guide management and maintenance decision making and prioritization. This dataset is a polygon representation of the Landscape Typologies within parks owned and maintained by DPR with the City and County of Denver (CCD). The Landscape Typology mapping and assessment effort was not comprehensive and did not include all areas maintained by DPR but focused on parks with natural vegetation communities. The general methodology for vegetation community mapping and scoring was as follows: DPR maintenance boundaries were used for park extents. Impervious surfaces, planting beds, and ball fields were clipped from the boundary. Vegetation communities were delineated using high-resolution aerial imagery. Polygons were mapped at a scale of 1/4 th acre for upland areas and 1/6 th acre for riparian areas. Vegetation community types and extents were field verified and adjusted as needed. Field data collection included recording the percent cover by each strata (trees, shrubs, forbs, and grasses), the two dominant vegetation species for each strata and their total cover, and the two dominant noxious weeds and their total cover. Additionally qualitative and semi-quantitative parameters were also scored in the field for each park that was assessed. Function (FUNC_PERCENT) was calculated by summing scores from each assessed parameter and dividing by the total possible score to get a normalized functional score. FUNCTION is based on the following thresholds: Excellent: 86-100 Good: 70-85 Fair: 50-69 Poor: <50 Restoration Score (RESTORATION SCORE PERCENT) was calculated by summing scores from each assessed ecological parameter (DIVERSITY SCORE, WILFLIFE SCORE, POLLINATOR HABITAT SCORE, NOXIOUS POPULATION SCORE, and INVASIVE WEED SCORE) and dividing by the total possible score to get a normalized restoration functional score. CUSP POLYGONS are polygons within +/- 2 points of a higher or lower function (FUNC_PERCENT). CUSP PRIORITY was assigned based on the type of cusp (risk of falling to lower function or ability to increase to higher function): Excellent à Good: Low Priority (1) Good à Excellent: Low Priority (1) Good à Fair: High Priority (5) Fair à Good: Moderate Priority (3) Fair à Poor: High Priority (5) Poor à Fair: High Priority (5)
semantic_summary: This dataset maps Denver Parks and Recreation's landscape typologies and functional assessments within city parks. It tracks park landscape types, functional and restoration scores, dominant vegetation species, noxious weed presence, and ecological parameters including diversity, wildlife, and pollinator habitat. Users can identify which parks require management prioritization based on their landscape types, functional scores, restoration needs, or noxious weed cover.

RNOs in the city’s official RNO database have active registrations and are listed with an “Active” status. Organizations that fail to renew by January 31 are marked “Inactive,” are excluded from the city’s official RNO database, and remain only as historical records for reference.
